title: Milne’s rationality conjecture and algebraic specialization
one_line_claim: Proves Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties over Q̄ with good reduction: specialized Hodge classes pair rationally with complementary divisor products, independently of cohomology theory.
problem_status_before: Milne's conjecture (2000s); specialist question in the Hodge/Tate comparison program
rating_reason: Specialist-famous conjecture in arithmetic geometry; feeds the CM Hodge result but is not widely known outside the area.
notable_flags: Depends on family 032 for the algebraic-cycle statement.

title: The full BSD formula from low Selmer corank
one_line_claim: Proves the full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over ℚ whose full q-power Selmer group has corank zero or one for some prime q, including finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group.
problem_status_before: BSD posed 1960s, a Millennium Problem; rank 0/1 equalities known since Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin, but the full leading-term formula only for restricted curves and primes
rating_reason: Would give the full BSD formula for every curve with Selmer corank ≤1, essentially everything in BSD short of rank ≥2.
notable_flags: Unformalized. Combined with 006 claims BSD for 100% of quadratic twists. Rank ≥2 untouched, so not the Millennium Problem itself.

title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
one_line_claim: Proves that every Dirichlet L-function, including ζ(s), is zero-free in Re s> 7/8, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
problem_status_before: No zero-free half-plane Re s > 1−δ known since Riemann (1859); no Siegel-zero exclusion known; considered far beyond current methods
rating_reason: A fixed zero-free half-plane for ζ and all Dirichlet L-functions (and no Landau–Siegel zeros) would be the biggest advance toward RH ever made.
verification: Lean, headline formalized; independent re-check in progress
notable_flags: Lean: Comparator challenge states Mathlib's riemannZeta s ≠ 0 for Re s > 7/8 with only standard axioms, a faithful statement (checked by me, not built). README: produced outside the fixed procedure and the 11/12 write-up was human-edited. Extraordinary claim: needs independent kernel check and expert reading. Comparator statement read by researcher6 (riemannZeta s ≠ 0 for Re s > 7/8); faithful to the claim. Independent Comparator re-check of the zeta statement was in progress at time of writing (CoolRmal/quasi-riemann-seven-eighths). Lichtman notes the proof relies on the cubic family of L-functions; an OpenAI team member says the method has a barrier at 3/4.

title: Hilbert’s tenth problem over ℚ
one_line_claim: Proves that no algorithm decides whether an integer-coefficient polynomial in an arbitrary number of variables has a rational zero, resolving Hilbert's tenth problem over ℚ negatively.
problem_status_before: Open since Matiyasevich (1970) settled the integer case; long-standing, widely known; Mazur's conjectures suggest Z is not existentially definable in Q
rating_reason: A negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over Q is one of the most sought-after results in logic/arithmetic geometry.
notable_flags: Unformalized. Must avoid an existential definition of Z in Q if Mazur's conjecture holds; method needs scrutiny. Pastén says it uses his group's height-growth idea for rank-one elliptic curves and wants to see the details.

title: Irrationality of Catalan’s constant
one_line_claim: Proves that Catalan's constant G=Σ_j≥0(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2 is irrational.
problem_status_before: Open since the 19th century; one of the best-known irrationality problems after ζ(3)
rating_reason: Irrationality of a famous classical constant; would be celebrated like Apéry's ζ(3).
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Shallit recalls an earlier LLM claim on Catalan's constant that proved too hasty (general caution, no specific error).

title: Goldfeld’s conjecture: densities and mean analytic rank
one_line_claim: Proves Goldfeld's conjecture for quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over ℚ: analytic ranks zero and one each have density 1/2, and the mean analytic rank tends to 1/2.
problem_status_before: Goldfeld 1979; Smith (2017–22) proved the 2-Selmer analogue for many curves; open in general
rating_reason: Settles the central conjecture on ranks in quadratic-twist families for every curve.

title: Ordinary two-point correlations and the corrected Elliott conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture, with a bound O(X/(log X)^c) for Liouville correlation sums along fixed nonproportional affine forms, where c &gt 0 is absolute.
problem_status_before: Chowla (1965) and Elliott; Tao (2015) proved the logarithmically averaged two-point case; ordinary case open
rating_reason: The non-averaged two-point Chowla conjecture is a flagship problem of multiplicative number theory.

title: The Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves that the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, with the Ihara bracket, is freely generated by one element in each odd weight 3, 5, 7, …, resolving the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture.
problem_status_before: Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture (~1990); Brown (2012) proved the motivic injectivity; freeness of grt open
rating_reason: A structural conjecture linking Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, multiple zeta values and motives.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (surprising for this subject; check scope).

title: Function-field reconstruction from Milnor K-theory and Galois data
one_line_claim: Reconstructs function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed constants from K^M_1/ell, K^M_2/ell, and their product.
problem_status_before: Bogomolov's birational anabelian program (1990s); partial results by Bogomolov–Tschinkel, Pop
rating_reason: Real progress in birational anabelian geometry, specialist interest.

title: Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two
one_line_claim: Every continuous odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation of G_ℚ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in a completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level.
problem_status_before: 2-adic Fontaine–Mazur for GL2/Q known only with residual hypotheses
rating_reason: Removing residual hypotheses at p=2 is a significant Langlands-program advance for specialists.

title: Prime-factor statistics of p-1
one_line_claim: Proves that the normalized ordered logarithms of the prime factors of p-1, counted with multiplicity, converge jointly to the Poisson–Dirichlet law PD(1) as p ranges uniformly over primes up to x and x→∞. This resolves the Ford–Konyagin–Luca conjecture.
problem_status_before: Ford–Konyagin–Luca conjecture; the n^{1−ε} totient-preimage statement is an old Erdős conjecture (best exponent ~0.71)
rating_reason: The Erdős totient-multiplicity consequence needs many smooth shifted primes, a well-known hard problem.

title: Independent largest prime factors of consecutive integers
one_line_claim: Resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture: the logarithmic sizes of the largest prime factors of n and n+1 are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density.
problem_status_before: Erdős–Pomerance (1978); Teräväinen proved the logarithmic-density version
rating_reason: Settles a well-known Erdős problem on consecutive integers.

title: Ostmann’s inverse Goldbach conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves that no finite modification of the primes can be written as A+B with A,B⊂ℤ_≥0 each containing at least two elements.
problem_status_before: Ostmann (1968); well-known inverse Goldbach problem, partial results by Elsholtz
rating_reason: Resolves a classic additive-number-theory problem.

title: Restricted geometric Langlands, global Arthur enhancements, and generic Ramanujan
one_line_claim: Proves the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves over overline𝔽_q under the four stated Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses.
problem_status_before: Characteristic-zero geometric Langlands proved 2024 (Gaitsgory–Raskin et al.); restricted char-p version and function-field Ramanujan open in these generalities
rating_reason: Extends a landmark program to positive characteristic with Ramanujan consequences; heavy and specialist.
notable_flags: Unformalized; conditional parts (Arthur enhancements assume a decomposition).

title: Torus-packet equidistribution in prime, quartic, and sextic degrees
one_line_claim: Proves Haar equidistribution without escape of mass for complete volume-weighted torus packets from totally real fields: arbitrary lattices and prescribed local types in fixed prime degree at least five, arbitrary-order Picard packets in primitive quartic fields, and maximal-order ideal-class packets in primitive sextic fields.
problem_status_before: Higher-degree Duke-type equidistribution; cubic case by Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss–Michel–Venkatesh; general degree open
rating_reason: Hard homogeneous-dynamics/number-theory equidistribution in new degrees.

title: Zilber–Pink in abelian varieties and the Siegel threefold
one_line_claim: Proves the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture over Q̄: every irreducible subvariety has finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties relative to its smallest containing torsion coset.
problem_status_before: Zilber–Pink (2000s); abelian case open with partial results (Habegger–Pila)
rating_reason: Proves a central unlikely-intersections conjecture for all abelian varieties over Q̄.

title: The irrationality exponent of π is 2
one_line_claim: Proves that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2: for every ε &gt 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational p/q satisfies |π-p/q|≥ q^-2-ε. This also proves convergence of the Flint–Hills series Σ_n≥11/(n^3sin^2 n), with angles in radians.
problem_status_before: Best bound μ(π) ≤ 7.10 (Zeilberger–Zudilin 2020); exact value 2 expected but considered out of reach
rating_reason: Determining π's irrationality exponent exactly is a classic, widely known problem; also settles Flint Hills series convergence.

title: The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over global fields
one_line_claim: Proves the Margulis–Platonov conjecture over every global field, including function fields of characteristic two.
problem_status_before: Margulis–Platonov (1970s); proven for most groups, a few types and char 2 remained
rating_reason: Completes a classical conjecture on normal subgroups of arithmetic groups.

title: The local p-adic section conjecture and global consequences
one_line_claim: Proves that rational points on every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite extension of ℚp correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes of sections of its full arithmetic étale fundamental group.
problem_status_before: Grothendieck's section conjecture (1983); p-adic local version open; no curve over Q with rational points was known to satisfy it
rating_reason: First cases of Grothendieck's anabelian section conjecture over Q would be a landmark for anabelian geometry.

title: Squarefree quartics and power-free polynomial values
one_line_claim: Proves the squarefree-values conjecture for irreducible integer quartics with no fixed prime-square divisor: squarefree values on positive integers have the predicted positive Euler-product density.
problem_status_before: Erdős asked; cubics by Hooley (1967); quartics open for decades
rating_reason: Squarefree values of quartic polynomials is a classic hard sieve problem.

title: A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal’s function
one_line_claim: Answers Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question: every interval of Ck^2 consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most k distinct prime divisors, for an absolute constant C. The bound is uniform over prime sets and interval positions and removes the classical logarithmic loss.
problem_status_before: Iwaniec (1978) proved O(k² log² k); quadratic bound conjectured
rating_reason: Removes the log loss in a classical sieve function.

title: The weak inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves that for every real shift γ and finite-valued psi:ℕ→[0,∞), divergence of Σ_qphi(q)psi(q)/q implies ‖qx-gamma‖< psi(q) for infinitely many q, for almost every x.
problem_status_before: Koukoulopoulos–Maynard (2019) proved Duffin–Schaeffer; inhomogeneous version open
rating_reason: Natural extension of a recent Annals breakthrough.

title: Patterson's first moment for cubic Gauss sums
one_line_claim: Proves unconditionally the all-primary-prime form of Patterson’s first-moment asymptotic: normalized cubic Gauss sums over primary Eisenstein primes of norm at most X, including both conjugates, have an explicit positive main term of order X^5/6/log X. Every fixed nonzero prime-angle Fourier mode has smaller order.
problem_status_before: Patterson (1978); Dunn–Radziwiłł (2021) proved it under GRH
rating_reason: Unconditional Patterson bias for cubic Gauss sums.

title: An asymptotic formula for the number of totients
one_line_claim: Gives an asymptotic equivalent for the number V(x) of distinct totient values up to x, with a positive bounded phase-dependent factor determined by convergent arithmetic approximations.
problem_status_before: Ford (1998) found the order of magnitude of V(x); asymptotic open
rating_reason: Sharpens a classical counting function, with an oscillating factor rather than a constant.

title: Short Egyptian fractions
one_line_claim: Every rational a/b with 1≤ a< b is a sum of O(loglog b) distinct positive unit fractions.
problem_status_before: Erdős conjecture; Vose proved O(√log b)
rating_reason: Settles an Erdős problem on Egyptian fractions.

title: Positive lower density of large prime gaps
one_line_claim: For every fixed C &gt 0, a positive proportion of consecutive prime gaps exceed Clog p_n, throughout every sufficiently large initial segment of the primes.
problem_status_before: Erdős–Prachar question; Banks–Freiberg–Maynard partial results
rating_reason: Nice prime-gap distribution result.

title: Potential integral density on curve character varieties
one_line_claim: Resolves the determinant-one curve case of Litt's integral-density question.
problem_status_before: Recent question of Litt
rating_reason: Specialist arithmetic-geometry result.
notable_flags: Unformalized. Litt says this is a very special case of his conjecture, with stronger work in progress by his student.

title: Uniformly bounded components of Gaussian-prime graphs
one_line_claim: Proves the Gaussian moat conjecture: no infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have uniformly bounded steps.
problem_status_before: Gaussian moat problem (Gordon 1962, Gethner–Wagon–Wick 1998); popular, believed true, no approach known
rating_reason: A famous, easy-to-state problem that resisted all attempts.

title: Primitive roots for every admissible integer base
one_line_claim: Proves the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture for every integer a that is neither −1 nor a square.
problem_status_before: Artin (1927); known under GRH (Hooley 1967); unconditionally at most two exceptional primes (Heath-Brown 1986) but no single base known
rating_reason: Unconditional Artin infinitude for every base (e.g. 2) is one of the most famous open problems in number theory.
notable_flags: Unformalized. Lower bound x/(log x)² rather than Artin's density.

title: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields
one_line_claim: Proves the modularity conjecture for elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields: every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field is modular, with matching local parameters at every place.
problem_status_before: Open; Caraiani–Newton (2023) proved modularity for a positive proportion over some imaginary quadratic fields
rating_reason: Full modularity over every imaginary quadratic field is a major Langlands milestone.

title: Uchida’s conjecture for open homomorphisms of Galois groups
one_line_claim: Proves Uchida's conjecture: every continuous open homomorphism between Galois groups of possibly infinite solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields comes from a unique equivariant field embedding in the opposite direction.
problem_status_before: Uchida's conjecture in anabelian geometry; specialist
rating_reason: Extends Neukirch–Uchida to open homomorphisms.

title: Hodge and Kuga–Satake results for all projective K3 surfaces
one_line_claim: Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and codimension.
problem_status_before: Hodge conjecture (Millennium Problem) open for CM abelian varieties beyond low dimensions (Markman's Weil-type fourfold work 2025); Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields open
rating_reason: Hodge for all CM abelian varieties, with Tate over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties as consequences, would be historic.
notable_flags: Unformalized. README: produced outside the fixed procedure. Family title (K3) and description (CM abelian varieties) differ.

title: Iitaka subadditivity, variation, and logarithmic additivity
one_line_claim: Proves Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for smooth Fujiki-class-C manifolds with rational simple-normal-crossing boundaries.
problem_status_before: Iitaka's subadditivity conjecture C(n,m) (1970s) open in general; Campana's orbifold version open
rating_reason: Iitaka subadditivity in full is a central open problem of birational geometry.
verification: Lean, partial (only the negative-fiber branch; the main Iitaka subadditivity theorem is unformalized)
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (surprising for this subject; check scope).

title: Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity
one_line_claim: Using logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, proves log abundance in every dimension for normal compact Kähler log canonical pairs with effective rational boundary: an analytically nef ℚ-Cartier adjoint is semiample.
problem_status_before: Abundance conjecture open in dimension ≥4
rating_reason: Log abundance in every dimension would complete a core part of the minimal model program.

title: Log-canonical threefold abundance in numerical dimension one
one_line_claim: Proves log abundance for projective log canonical threefold pairs over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p &gt 3 when the effective boundary is rational and the ℚ-Cartier adjoint is nef of numerical dimension one.
problem_status_before: Char-p threefold abundance, partial results
rating_reason: Narrow case of positive-characteristic abundance.

title: Numerical semiampleness and generalized minimal models
one_line_claim: Proves numerical semiampleness for nef adjoints K_X+B+M with K_X+B pseudo-effective and M nef rational, for projective klt rational pairs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields and smooth compact Kähler rational klt simple-normal-crossing pairs, using Bott–Chern cohomology in the latter case.
problem_status_before: Existence of minimal models for lc pairs open in dimension ≥5
rating_reason: Minimal models for all pseudo-effective generalized lc pairs would settle a central MMP conjecture.

title: The ordinary-double-point volume gap
one_line_claim: Proves the ordinary-double-point volume-gap conjecture: every singular complex algebraic klt germ of dimension n ≥ 2, with zero boundary, has normalized volume at most 2(n-1)^n.
problem_status_before: Spotti–Sun conjecture; known in dimension ≤3
rating_reason: Solid K-stability result.

title: Fujita’s freeness conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves Fujita's freeness conjecture at its sharp bound in every dimension: for a smooth projective complex variety X of dimension n and an ample line bundle L, the adjoint K_X+mL is globally generated for every integer m≥ n+1.
problem_status_before: Fujita (1985); known in dimension ≤5
rating_reason: A famous, decades-old conjecture in algebraic geometry.

title: Nagata’s conjecture and maximal Seshadri constants
one_line_claim: Proves Nagata's strict inequality Σ_i m_i< d√ r for every nonzero effective plane curve of degree d through r ≥ 10 very general complex points, with arbitrary multiplicities mi.
problem_status_before: Nagata (1959); known only when r is a square
rating_reason: Famous half-century-old conjecture on plane curves.

title: Bloch’s conjecture for complex surfaces
one_line_claim: Proves Bloch's conjecture: for every smooth connected projective complex surface S with p_g(S)=0, the Albanese map CH_0(S)^0→Alb(S)(ℂ) on integral degree-zero zero-cycles is an isomorphism.
problem_status_before: Bloch (1976); known for Kodaira dimension <2 and special surfaces of general type
rating_reason: Central conjecture on algebraic cycles for surfaces.
notable_flags: Unformalized. Issue reported: Daniel Litt (Toronto) on X, 6 Oct 23:38 UTC, says the Bloch paper cites some incorrect existing work without noting it, but that it does not seem to rely on it meaningfully (x.com/littmath/status/2107616410897678765).

title: Hyperkähler SYZ and projective-space bases
one_line_claim: Proves the strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture: every holomorphic line bundle with nonzero nef isotropic first Chern class on a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic Kähler manifold is semiample.
problem_status_before: Strong SYZ and Matsushita base conjecture open; base P^n known only for smooth base (Hwang 2008)
rating_reason: Major structural results for hyperkähler manifolds.

title: Oka classification for minimal compact complex surfaces: Kodaira dimension zero and class VII
one_line_claim: Proves that every complex K3 surface is Oka, including nonprojective surfaces.
problem_status_before: Whether K3 surfaces are Oka was a well-known open question in Oka theory
rating_reason: Long-standing question in complex analysis/geometry.

title: P = W for fixed-determinant SLn moduli spaces
one_line_claim: Proves P_k=W_2k=W_2k+1 on the full rational cohomology of smooth coprime fixed-determinant, trace-free Higgs moduli spaces and their character varieties for composite ranks over smooth projective complex curves of genus at least two.
problem_status_before: P = W proved 2022 for GL_n; SL_n fixed-determinant composite rank open
rating_reason: Completes a recent major theorem in a remaining case.

title: The equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves the equivariant cohomological Hikita correspondence for every finite quiver, including loops and multiple arrows, with arbitrary dimension and framing vectors and commuting flavor torus.
problem_status_before: Hikita conjecture in symplectic duality; partial cases known
rating_reason: Specialist geometric representation theory.

title: Shafarevich counterexamples in dimension two and with large fundamental group
one_line_claim: Constructs a smooth projective complex fourfold with large fundamental group whose universal cover contains no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety but is neither Stein nor holomorphically convex.
problem_status_before: Shafarevich holomorphic-convexity conjecture (1970s); Bogomolov–Katzarkov suggested conditional counterexamples
rating_reason: Disproves a classical conjecture on universal covers.

title: Zariski cancellation and affine fibrations over the complex numbers
one_line_claim: Constructs an integral complex affine fourfold Xnot≅𝔸^4 with X×𝔸^1≅𝔸^5, disproving affine-space cancellation over ℂ in dimension four.
problem_status_before: Zariski cancellation over C open for n ≥ 3; Gupta (2014) disproved it in positive characteristic
rating_reason: A char-0 counterexample would be a landmark in affine algebraic geometry.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (counterexamples are well suited to formal checking).

title: A characteristic-zero counterexample to Lipman–Zariski
one_line_claim: Constructs a singular normal affine complex surface with free rank-two tangent sheaf, disproving the characteristic-zero Lipman–Zariski conjecture.
problem_status_before: Lipman–Zariski (1965); proven for klt and other classes
rating_reason: Surprising char-0 counterexample to a classical conjecture.

title: A stable-coordinate counterexample in four variables
one_line_claim: Constructs a polynomial in four complex variables that is not a coordinate but becomes one after adjoining a single variable, disproving the Stable Coordinate conjecture in four variables.
problem_status_before: Stable coordinate and Abhyankar–Sathaye conjectures open in dimension ≥3
rating_reason: Counterexamples to well-known affine-geometry conjectures.

title: A counterexample to Griffiths’ positivity conjecture
one_line_claim: Constructs ample rank-two bundles on ℙ^1×ℙ^1 with no smooth Hermitian metric of strictly Griffiths-positive curvature, disproving Griffiths' positivity conjecture already on the quadric surface.
problem_status_before: Griffiths (1969) conjecture: ample implies Griffiths positive
rating_reason: Counterexample to a classical complex-geometry conjecture.

title: Kobayashi’s canonical-ampleness conjecture
one_line_claim: Every compact connected Kähler manifold of positive complex dimension with no nonconstant entire curve has ample canonical bundle and is therefore projective.
problem_status_before: Kobayashi (1970) conjecture; open in dimension ≥3
rating_reason: Hyperbolic compact Kähler implies ample canonical bundle is a famous conjecture.

title: Tangent splittings and product decompositions
one_line_claim: A splitting of the tangent bundle of a compact Kähler manifold into two integrable holomorphic subbundles induces a compatible product decomposition of its universal cover, proving the two-summand form of Beauville's splitting conjecture.
problem_status_before: Beauville splitting conjecture; Höring's conjecture
rating_reason: Solid structural result in Kähler geometry.

title: A counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow
one_line_claim: Constructs a tautological relation on a moduli space of stable pointed curves that vanishes in rational Chow, hence in rational cohomology, but lies outside Pixton's original relation span.
problem_status_before: Pixton's completeness conjecture for tautological relations
rating_reason: Counterexample to a prominent moduli-of-curves conjecture.

title: Irrational cubic fourfolds with Hodge-theoretic and categorical K3 associations
one_line_claim: For every sufficiently large admissible Hassett discriminant, a very general smooth complex cubic fourfold is irrational despite having both an untwisted geometric K3 category and an integral Hodge-theoretic K3 association.
problem_status_before: Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture for cubic fourfolds; irrationality of any cubic fourfold unproven classically (Kontsevich et al. Hodge-atom claim 2025)
rating_reason: Irrational cubic fourfolds with associated K3 would overturn the main expectation in the area.

title: Gepner symmetry and large-volume stability on threefolds
one_line_claim: Proves Toda's Gepner conjecture for every smooth complex quintic threefold, constructing a numerical Bridgeland stability condition with the prescribed phase shift 2/5.
problem_status_before: Toda's Gepner conjecture; existence of stability conditions on Calabi–Yau threefolds a major open problem
rating_reason: Stability conditions on all CY3s at large volume would be a big step.

title: Termination of projective and Kähler fourfold minimal model programs
one_line_claim: Proves termination of every existing generalized log canonical flip sequence on globally Weil ℚ-factorial compact Kähler fourfolds, with rational boundary, fixed rational analytically nef b-data, and projective small flip diagrams with the prescribed ample signs.
problem_status_before: Termination of lc flips in dimension 4 partially known
rating_reason: Advances MMP termination in dimension four.

title: Fundamental groups of special complex varieties and root orbifolds
one_line_claim: Proves Campana's abelianity conjecture: special compact Kähler manifolds have virtually abelian fundamental groups.
problem_status_before: Campana's abelianity conjecture (2004)
rating_reason: A well-known conjecture on special manifolds.

title: Semialgebraic universal covers and bounded domains
one_line_claim: Proves the Kollár–Pardon conjecture: the semialgebraic universal covers of connected normal projective complex varieties are exactly products D×ℂ^m× F, with D bounded symmetric and F simply connected, normal, and projective.
problem_status_before: Kollár–Pardon conjecture (2012)
rating_reason: Classification of semialgebraic universal covers.

title: Counterexamples to Zariski’s multiplicity conjecture
one_line_claim: Disproves Zariski's multiplicity conjecture by constructing reduced holomorphic hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic but have different multiplicities.
problem_status_before: Zariski's multiplicity question (1971), one of the best-known problems in singularity theory
rating_reason: Counterexample to a famous half-century-old conjecture.

title: The Global Spherical Shell conjecture
one_line_claim: Every connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII with b_2> 0 contains a global spherical shell, proving the positive-b2 Global Spherical Shell conjecture.
problem_status_before: Kato/Nakamura GSS conjecture; Teleman proved b2 ≤ 3
rating_reason: Would finish the classification of class VII surfaces, the last gap in Kodaira's classification.

title: Projective contact classification and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture: every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kähler manifold of real dimension at least eight is homothetic to a compact symmetric Wolf space.
problem_status_before: LeBrun–Salamon (1991); known in low dimensions
rating_reason: Famous rigidity conjecture in quaternionic-Kähler geometry.

title: The generalized Mukai conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves the generalized Mukai conjecture: every positive-dimensional smooth complex projective Fano manifold of dimension n, Picard number ρ and pseudoindex ι satisfies rho(iota-1)≤ n, with equality exactly for (ℙ^iota-1)^rho.
problem_status_before: Generalized Mukai conjecture (Bonavero et al.); known in low dimensions
rating_reason: Solid Fano-geometry result.

title: Topological triviality of μ-constant surface singularities
one_line_claim: Proves topological right-triviality for every holomorphic one-parameter family of isolated hypersurface singularities in ℂ3 with constant Milnor number, resolving the surface case of the μ-constant problem.
problem_status_before: Lê–Ramanujam (1976) handled all dimensions except surfaces in C³
rating_reason: Settles the famous exceptional case of the μ-constant problem.

title: Virasoro constraints for complete intersections and projective-bundle towers
one_line_claim: Proves the full ordinary unreduced descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in complex projective space, in every genus and curve class with arbitrary cohomology insertions.
problem_status_before: Virasoro conjecture (1997) known for toric varieties, curves, some homogeneous spaces
rating_reason: Big Gromov–Witten advance for complete intersections.

title: Bounded klt complements for Fano contractions
one_line_claim: Proves the finite-rational-coefficient form of Shokurov’s bounded-klt-complement conjecture for ϵ-lc complex Fano-type pairs with nef anti-log-canonical divisor.
problem_status_before: Shokurov's bounded complements; Birkar proved the main case
rating_reason: Specialist MMP result.

title: The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six
one_line_claim: Proves the Campana–Peternell conjecture in complex dimension six: every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.
problem_status_before: Campana–Peternell conjecture known up to dimension 5
rating_reason: One more dimension of a known conjecture.

title: Anticanonical nonvanishing in every dimension
one_line_claim: If X is a smooth connected complex projective variety and -K_X admits a smooth Hermitian metric with nonnegative curvature, then H^0(X,-mK_X)≠0 for some m &gt 0.
problem_status_before: Nonvanishing for semipositive anticanonical bundles
rating_reason: Specialist complex-geometry result.

title: Global quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level
one_line_claim: Proves the unramified de Rham quantum geometric Langlands equivalence for every connected simple complex algebraic group on every smooth projective connected complex curve, at every shifted level c∈ℂ∖ℚ.
problem_status_before: Quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level, recent program (Gaitsgory et al.)
rating_reason: Major Langlands-program result for specialists.

title: Koebe’s circle-domain conjecture
one_line_claim: Resolves the existence part of Koebe's circle-domain conjecture: every domain in the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a domain whose complementary components are round disks or points.
problem_status_before: Koebe's Kreisnormierungsproblem (1908); He–Schramm (1993) countably many boundary components
rating_reason: A century-old, famous problem in conformal mapping.

title: Brennan's conjecture and the integral-means spectrum
one_line_claim: Proves Brennan's conjecture: for every conformal bijection ϕ from a simply connected plane domain onto the disk, |phi'|^s is area-integrable for 4/3< s< 4.
problem_status_before: Brennan (1978); integral-means spectrum conjectures open
rating_reason: Well-known conjecture in geometric function theory.

title: The Falconer distance conjecture
one_line_claim: Resolves the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension d ≥ 2: every compact set E⊂ℝ^d with Hausdorff dimension greater than d/2 determines a set of Euclidean distances of positive Lebesgue measure.
problem_status_before: Falconer (1985); best thresholds d/2 + 1/4 (plane) and similar
rating_reason: Settles a famous geometric-measure-theory conjecture in all dimensions.
verification: Lean, headline formalized; independently re-checked (Comparator pass)
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (surprising for this subject). Independent Comparator re-check PASSED (Yongxi Lin, CMU, GitHub CoolRmal, finished 7 Oct 00:07 UTC, default kernel, Landrun sandbox).

title: Kakeya in three and four dimensions
one_line_claim: Resolves the Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions and the Hausdorff-dimension conjecture in four.
problem_status_before: Wang–Zahl (2025) proved 3D Kakeya set dimension; 3D maximal conjecture and 4D dimension open
rating_reason: Kakeya in 4D and the 3D maximal function are top harmonic-analysis problems.

title: The Llog L Fourier-convergence conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves that the ordinary symmetric Fourier partial sums of every complex-valued function in Llog L(𝕋) converge almost everywhere along the full sequence.
problem_status_before: Classical; Antonov (1996) proved L log L log log log L
rating_reason: Classic problem on Fourier series convergence.

title: Real ultraflat Littlewood polynomials and unbounded binary merit factors
one_line_claim: Constructs polynomials with N consecutive coefficients in {-1,1} whose modulus is (1+o(1))√ N uniformly on the entire unit circle, for every sufficiently large integer length N. Thus real Littlewood polynomials are ultraflat, including at the real endpoints.
problem_status_before: Erdős conjectured no ultraflat ±1 polynomials; flat ones found 2019 (Balister et al.); Turyn's bounded merit factor conjecture
rating_reason: Refuting Erdős's ultraflatness conjecture and Golay/Turyn merit factor bounds would be a sensation.

title: Fourier restriction for positively curved surfaces
one_line_claim: Proves the diagonal Fourier extension conjecture for positively curved surfaces in three dimensions.
problem_status_before: Stein's restriction conjecture in R³ open since the 1960s–70s; central to harmonic analysis
rating_reason: The 3D restriction conjecture for curved surfaces implies Kakeya and would be field-defining.

title: The three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture
one_line_claim: Resolves the three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture in its strict range: the Bochner–Riesz multipliers of order δ are bounded on L^p(ℝ^3) for every 1≤ p≤∞ whenever δ> max{3|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0}.
problem_status_before: Bochner–Riesz conjecture open in dimension ≥3
rating_reason: A classic central conjecture of harmonic analysis.

title: Local smoothing in three dimensions
one_line_claim: Resolves Sogge's local smoothing conjecture for the Euclidean wave equation in three spatial dimensions.
problem_status_before: Sogge (1991); proved in 2D by Guth–Wang–Zhang (2020); 3D open
rating_reason: Top-tier harmonic analysis result.

title: The exact Sobolev endpoint for Schrödinger convergence
one_line_claim: Proves almost-everywhere convergence e^itΔf→ f as tdownarrow0 for every f∈ H^n/(2(n+1))(ℝ^n) and every dimension n ≥ 2.
problem_status_before: Du–Zhang (2019) proved s > n/(2(n+1)); endpoint open
rating_reason: Endpoint of a recently solved problem.

title: Riesz transforms and rectifiability in higher codimension
one_line_claim: Resolves the remaining higher-codimension Riesz-transform rectifiability problem: for d ≥ 4 and 2≤ n≤ d-2, an n-Ahlfors–David regular Radon measure on ℝd is uniformly n-rectifiable whenever its n-dimensional Riesz transform is uniformly L2-bounded over all positive hard truncations.
problem_status_before: David–Semmes problem in higher codimension; codimension 1 by Nazarov–Tolsa–Volberg
rating_reason: Completes a major geometric-measure-theory program.

title: Annular variation and dyadic absolute bounds for the triangular Hilbert transform
one_line_claim: Proves maximal and annular r-variation bounds, for every r &gt 2, from complex L^3(ℝ^2)× L^3(ℝ^2) to L^3/2(ℝ^2).
problem_status_before: Triangular Hilbert transform boundedness, a well-known open problem
rating_reason: Settles the central L³ point of a famous open problem.

title: Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz directions
one_line_claim: Proves a uniform strong L2 bound for the planar Hilbert transform along any Lipschitz unit vector field, at integration lengths bounded by an absolute multiple of its reciprocal Lipschitz constant.
problem_status_before: Stein's conjecture on Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz vector fields (1980s)
rating_reason: A famous long-open harmonic-analysis conjecture at its key scale.

title: The geometric case of the Erdős similarity conjecture
one_line_claim: For every fixed q∈(0,1), constructs compact subsets of [0,1] with measure arbitrarily close to one containing no translated and nontrivially dilated copy of {q^n:n≥1}, with dilations of either sign.
problem_status_before: Erdős similarity conjecture (1974); geometric-sequence case open
rating_reason: Settles the best-known open case of an Erdős problem.

title: Endpoint Sobolev regularity of centered disk averages
one_line_claim: Resolves the planar centered-disk case of the Hajłasz–Onninen maximal-function regularity problem.
problem_status_before: Hajłasz–Onninen problem (2004)
rating_reason: Specialist regularity result.

title: An L3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform
one_line_claim: Proves that the principal-value trilinear Hilbert transform with shifts x-t, x-2t, x-3t is bounded from L^3(ℝ)^3 to L^1(ℝ).
problem_status_before: Trilinear Hilbert transform boundedness open
rating_reason: Partial progress on a well-known problem.

title: The Mahler conjectures, functional inequalities and polar-product symplectic width
one_line_claim: Resolves the symmetric and nonsymmetric geometric Mahler conjectures in every dimension, with Hanner polytopes and simplices as the respective volume-product minimizers and all equality cases classified.
problem_status_before: Mahler (1939); proved only in dimensions ≤3 (Iriyeh–Shibata 2020)
rating_reason: A famous convex-geometry conjecture in all dimensions with equality cases, plus a symplectic consequence.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Reasoning trace released. Comparator statement read by researcher6 (symmetric Mahler 4^n/n! lower bound); faithful to the claim.

title: Sharp projection-body inequalities and a counterexample to simplex maximization
one_line_claim: Proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in the remaining dimensions n ≥ 4: ellipsoids uniquely minimize projection-body volume at fixed body volume.
problem_status_before: Petty's conjectured projection inequality (1971)
rating_reason: Settles a classical convex-geometry conjecture.

title: Bounded-distortion L1 embeddings of planar and bounded-treewidth graphs
one_line_claim: Resolves the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture.
problem_status_before: Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture (1999)
rating_reason: The planar case is a famous metric-embedding problem with algorithmic consequences.

title: Triangular-lattice optimality, long-range Riesz and Coulomb energies, and spherical logarithmic energy
one_line_claim: Proves that the triangular lattice minimizes the lower limit of energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone potential of squared distance among locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one.
problem_status_before: Cohn–Kumar universal optimality of the hexagonal lattice in 2D open (proved in dimensions 8 and 24)
rating_reason: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice in the plane is a famous problem.

title: Logarithmic and Lp Brunn–Minkowski inequalities and the B-conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality for origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension, and the scalar-dilation B-conjecture for all even log-concave Radon measures.
problem_status_before: Log-Brunn–Minkowski conjecture (Böröczky–Lutwak–Yang–Zhang 2012); B-conjecture (Latała 2002)
rating_reason: Central conjectures of modern convex geometry.

title: The optimal order of convex-body covering density
one_line_claim: Determines the optimal worst-case covering density as Theta(nlog n), for both lattice and unrestricted translative coverings.
problem_status_before: Rogers (1950s) upper bounds; no superlinear lower bound known
rating_reason: A matching n log n lower bound would be new and striking.

title: Dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for subgaussian log-concave measures
one_line_claim: Proves a dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for centered log-concave densities with uniformly subgaussian linear marginals, with constant bounded by a universal multiple of the squared linear subgaussian parameter.
problem_status_before: Related to KLS (Chen, Klartag)
rating_reason: Solid high-dimensional probability result.

title: Subpolynomial dimension reduction in Lp
one_line_claim: For every fixed 1< p< ∞ and distortion D &gt 1, every n-point subset of real Lp embeds into ell_p^d with distortion at most D and dimension d=n^o(1), answering Naor's sublinear-dimension question for p ≠ 2.
problem_status_before: Naor's question for Lp, p ≠ 2
rating_reason: Answers a well-known metric-embedding question.

title: Hyperbolicity cones without semidefinite lifts
one_line_claim: Disproves the Projected Lax conjecture: some hyperbolicity cones are not spectrahedral shadows.
problem_status_before: Generalized Lax conjecture (2000s), a central question in real algebraic geometry and optimization
rating_reason: Disproof shows hyperbolic programming is strictly more expressive than semidefinite programming.

title: The Gaussian propeller conjecture in every dimension
one_line_claim: Proves that the sum of squared Gaussian first moments of any finite measurable partition is at most 9/(8π).
problem_status_before: Khot–Naor (2008); proved in dimension 3
rating_reason: Settles a geometric conjecture; complexity consequence depends on 102.

title: The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström bound
one_line_claim: Proves that any finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝd admits signs keeping every partial sum within C√ d, independently of length.
problem_status_before: Euclidean Steinitz constant √d conjectured; best general bounds involve log n
rating_reason: A well-known discrepancy-theory conjecture.

title: Compact counterexamples to bi-Lipschitz dimension reduction
one_line_claim: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling set that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space.
problem_status_before: Lang–Plaut problem (2001)
rating_reason: Answers a known metric-geometry question.

title: The sharp exponential scale of edit-distance distortion
one_line_claim: Determines the least distortion of embedding edit distance on words of length at most d into real ℓ1: it is exp(Theta(√log dloglog d)).
problem_status_before: Gap between Krauthgamer–Rabani lower bound and Ostrovsky–Rabani upper bound since 2005
rating_reason: Closes a well-known gap in metric embeddings.

title: Cylinder coverings below the half-area bound
one_line_claim: Covers the entire closed regular tetrahedron by finitely many cylinders with compact triangular perpendicular bases whose total area is less than half its smallest orthogonal projection area.
problem_status_before: Bang-type cylinder covering conjecture
rating_reason: Niche convex-geometry counterexample.

title: The sharp simplex conjecture for isotropic constants
one_line_claim: Proves that simplices uniquely maximize the isotropic constant among convex bodies in every dimension, resolving the strong isotropic constant conjecture.
problem_status_before: Strong isotropic constant conjecture; Klartag (2024) proved boundedness
rating_reason: Sharp form of the slicing problem.

title: The Unique Games Conjecture and optimal approximation thresholds
one_line_claim: Proves Khot's Unique Games Conjecture.
problem_status_before: Khot's Unique Games Conjecture (2002); 2-to-2 theorem (2018)
rating_reason: Proving UGC would settle optimal approximability of a huge class of problems; prize-level.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (check scope; extraordinary for a PCP-type proof). Reasoning trace released. Comparator statement read by researcher6 (3SAT → affine unique games over F_2^s, completeness 1−ε, soundness δ); faithful to the claim. HN readers call the notation painful (exposition, not an error).

title: Exact derandomization of logarithmic space: mathsf L=RL=BPL
one_line_claim: Proves mathsf L=RL=BPL, resolving derandomization for bounded-error logarithmic-space computation.
problem_status_before: Saks–Zhou (1999) BPL ⊆ L^{3/2}; small improvements since; full derandomization considered far off
rating_reason: Unconditional L = BPL would be a landmark of complexity theory.

title: Quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games
one_line_claim: Gives deterministic algorithms using 2^O((log(L+2))^2) bit operations, for complete binary input length L, for ordinary mean-payoff games and two separate extensions.
problem_status_before: Parity games in quasipolynomial time since 2017; mean-payoff and simple stochastic games not known to be in QP
rating_reason: Quasipolynomial mean-payoff and stochastic games would be a major algorithmic advance on a decades-old NP∩coNP problem.

title: Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games
one_line_claim: Proves Khot's 2-to-1 Games Conjecture with perfect completeness: for every fixed rational δ∈(0,1), it is NP-hard to distinguish satisfiable games from games whose optimum is at most δ, on explicit unweighted instances.
problem_status_before: Khot's 2-to-1 conjecture with perfect completeness open; 2-to-2 theorem (2018) has imperfect completeness
rating_reason: A central hardness-of-approximation conjecture; implies strong coloring hardness.

title: Hardness of coloring three-colorable graphs
one_line_claim: It is NP-hard to color a three-colorable graph using any fixed number c ≥ 3 of colors.
problem_status_before: Best known: 5-coloring 3-colorable graphs NP-hard (Bulín–Krokhin–Opršal 2019); constant c open for decades
rating_reason: Settles a famous approximate-coloring problem.

title: Matrix multiplication with exponent at most 9/4
one_line_claim: Proves ω≤9/4 over ℂ, giving O_ε(n^9/4+ε) arithmetic operations for square matrix multiplication.
problem_status_before: ω < 2.3714 (Alman–Duan–Vassilevska Williams–Xu–Xu–Zhou 2024); progress since 1990 in tiny steps
rating_reason: A jump from ~2.371 to 2.25 would be the largest advance in matrix multiplication since Strassen-era methods.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (check scope; a laser-method-scale formalization would itself be remarkable). Comparator statement read by researcher6 (ω(ℂ) ≤ 9/4 for division-free algebraic programs); faithful to the claim.

title: A cubic permanent–determinant lower bound
one_line_claim: Proves an Omega(n^3) lower bound for the border determinantal complexity of the n× n permanent over ℂ.
problem_status_before: Best bounds quadratic (Mignon–Ressayre 2004; Landsberg–Manivel–Ressayre for border)
rating_reason: A cubic bound would be the first real advance on permanent vs determinant in two decades.

title: Integer multiplication below nlog n
one_line_claim: Multiplies two n-bit integers exactly at every input length in deterministic worst-case time O(n(log n)^1-κ), with κ=2^-182, on one fixed finite-alphabet Turing machine with finitely many one-dimensional tapes.
problem_status_before: Harvey–van der Hoeven (2019) achieved n log n, conjectured optimal
rating_reason: Beating n log n would overturn a widely believed optimality conjecture.

title: Optimal-order randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics
one_line_claim: Establishes a randomized competitive ratio O(log^2(k+1)) for k-server on every metric space, matching the worst-case lower-bound order.
problem_status_before: Bubeck–Coester–Rabani (2023) refuted the polylog conjecture's O(log k) form with an Ω(log² k) lower bound
rating_reason: Matching O(log² k) on all metrics would close the randomized k-server problem.

title: One-sample matroid prophet inequalities against an almighty adversary
one_line_claim: For every finite matroid known in advance, gives a distribution-independent online rule using one independent sample per element and earning a universal constant fraction of the expected offline optimum.
problem_status_before: Recent prophet-inequality questions
rating_reason: Solid online-algorithms result.

title: Beyond the square-root exponent for depth-three circuits
one_line_claim: Constructs a single language in deterministic polynomial time whose n-bit membership function requires 2^ω(√ n) total gates in unbounded-fan-in OR–AND–OR circuits, at every sufficiently large input length.
problem_status_before: Håstad-type 2^Ω(√n) barrier for depth-3 circuits since the 1980s
rating_reason: Crossing the square-root barrier is a long-sought circuit lower bound.

title: Approximate counting and entropy of perfect matchings
one_line_claim: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings in arbitrary finite simple graphs, with exact detection of zero counts.
problem_status_before: Jerrum–Sinclair–Vigoda (2004) did bipartite graphs; general graphs a famous open problem
rating_reason: An FPRAS for perfect matchings in general graphs is a celebrated open problem in counting.

title: Approximate counting of common integer polymatroid bases
one_line_claim: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting common integer bases of two integral polymatroids of equal total rank, supplied by exact rank-value oracles.
problem_status_before: Counting common bases of two matroids is a known open problem generalizing bipartite matchings
rating_reason: Significant approximate-counting result.

title: Sampling and counting contingency tables with arbitrary margins
one_line_claim: For nonnegative integer matrices with prescribed row and column sums, gives exact uniform sampling in expected polynomial bit time and almost-uniform sampling in worst-case polynomial bit time.
problem_status_before: Contingency-table sampling known only for restricted margins (Diaconis et al.)
rating_reason: Solid sampling result with statistics applications.

title: Uniform black-box noncommutative identity testing across characteristics
one_line_claim: For each characteristic, constructs in deterministic polynomial bit time a polynomial-dimensional matrix tuple detecting every nonzero division-free noncommutative formula of bounded size over any field of that characteristic.
problem_status_before: Black-box noncommutative rational identity testing open
rating_reason: Solid derandomization result.

title: Uniform sparsest cut: hardness and semidefinite gaps
one_line_claim: Proves that approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any fixed constant factor is NP-hard, even with nonnegative rational capacities and unit demands.
problem_status_before: Constant-factor hardness of uniform sparsest cut known only under strong conjectures
rating_reason: Unconditional NP-hardness for a central graph-partitioning problem.

title: Bin packing and unbounded configuration-LP gaps
one_line_claim: Disproves the modified integer round-up conjecture of Scheithauer and Terno: the integral bin-packing optimum can exceed its configuration linear-programming value by an arbitrarily large additive constant.
problem_status_before: MIRUP conjecture (Scheithauer–Terno 1995); OPT+O(1) bin packing on Williamson–Shmoys's top open-problem list
rating_reason: Settles a famous approximation-algorithms question negatively.

title: The Courtade–Kumar and Hellinger conjectures
one_line_claim: Proves the Courtade–Kumar conjecture: among Boolean functions of independent uniform bits, a single coordinate retains the most mutual information after independent bit-flip noise.
problem_status_before: Courtade–Kumar (2014), a well-known information-theory conjecture
rating_reason: Settles the 'most informative Boolean function' question.

title: Almost-linear-time exact matching and prescribed-degree factors in general graphs
one_line_claim: Gives a randomized algorithm finding an exact maximum-cardinality matching in any simple undirected graph in (n+m)^1+o(1) word time, with success probability at least 2/3.
problem_status_before: Almost-linear max-flow (2022) gave bipartite matching; general-graph matching almost-linear open
rating_reason: Almost-linear maximum matching in general graphs would be a top algorithms result.

title: Almost-linear approximation of edit distance
one_line_claim: For every fixed rational ε∈(0,1), gives a randomized (1+ε) approximation to unit-cost edit distance in worst-case expected time N^1+o(1), with success probability at least 2/3.
problem_status_before: Andoni–Nosatzki constant-factor near-linear; (1+ε) open
rating_reason: Near-optimal edit-distance approximation.

title: Quantitative trace-reconstruction bounds with a uniform decoder
one_line_claim: At every fixed deletion probability in (0,1), reconstructing an arbitrary length-n binary string requires n^Omega(loglog n) independent traces, ruling out polynomial-sample reconstruction.
problem_status_before: Trace reconstruction: upper exp(Õ(n^{1/5})) (Chase 2021), lower ~n^{3/2}
rating_reason: Closing an exponential gap and ruling out polynomial reconstruction would be striking.

title: Polynomial-time scheduling on three identical machines
one_line_claim: Resolves the three-processor unit-job scheduling problem of Garey and Johnson: a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm minimizes makespan for nonpreemptive unit-length jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on three identical parallel machines.
problem_status_before: Garey–Johnson (1979) open problem; still open
rating_reason: Resolves one of the classic open problems in scheduling complexity.

title: The metric k-median approximation threshold and recovery
one_line_claim: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time (1+2/e+ε)-approximation for finite rational metric k-median with specified candidate facilities, for every fixed ε &gt 0.
problem_status_before: Best k-median approximation ~2.6; hardness 1+2/e
rating_reason: A tight approximation factor for a central clustering problem.

title: Exponential semidefinite complexity of perfect matching
one_line_claim: Proves that every exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope has exponential size, answering Rothvoss's polynomial-size lift question negatively.
problem_status_before: Rothvoss (2014) exponential LP extension complexity; SDP version open
rating_reason: Major extended-formulation lower bound.
verification: Lean, partial (superpolynomial, not exponential, bound formalized)

title: Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions
one_line_claim: Proves that a degree-at-most-d polynomial threshold function on the uniform n-dimensional Boolean cube has average sensitivity at most 8d√ n, uniformly for 1≤ d≤ n.
problem_status_before: Gotsman–Linial conjecture (1994)
rating_reason: Settles a well-known Boolean-function conjecture asymptotically.

title: A factor-two approximation for shortest common superstring
one_line_claim: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm constructing a common superstring of length at most twice the optimum for every finite family of explicitly represented strings.
problem_status_before: Greedy conjecture says 2; best proven ~2.47
rating_reason: Long-sought approximation factor.

title: Exponential state costs for two-way automata
one_line_claim: Proves exponential lower bounds both for complementing two-way nondeterministic finite automata and for simulating one-way nondeterministic automata by two-way deterministic ones.
problem_status_before: Sakoda–Sipser (1978), a famous automata problem
rating_reason: Partial resolution over growing alphabets.

title: Exact Fourier transforms below nlog n
one_line_claim: Gives a deterministic length-n discrete Fourier transform algorithm using O(n(log n)^1-δ) operations for every n, with explicit δ=10^-13.
problem_status_before: FFT's n log n believed optimal since 1965; lower bounds only for restricted models
rating_reason: Beating n log n for exact DFT would be a shock to algorithm theory.
verification: Lean, partial (only a subsequence of lengths with o(n log n) circuits, not every n)

title: Rapid mixing of graph switches for every degree sequence
one_line_claim: Resolves the simple-undirected Kannan–Tetali–Vempala conjecture: the lazy edge-switch chain mixes in O(n^8) time for every graphical labeled degree sequence.
problem_status_before: Kannan–Tetali–Vempala (1999) conjecture
rating_reason: Settles a known Markov-chain mixing problem.

title: A superquadratic separation of sensitivity and block sensitivity
one_line_claim: Constructs total Boolean functions with block sensitivity mathopbsnolimits (f)≥ s(f)^α for a fixed α &gt 2, disproving the quadratic strengthening of the Sensitivity Conjecture.
problem_status_before: Quadratic bs vs s conjecture after Huang's 2019 sensitivity theorem
rating_reason: Clarifies the sensitivity landscape.

title: The computational complexity of Weisfeiler–Leman refinement
one_line_claim: Proves unconditional n^Omega(k) deterministic time lower bounds for joint and separate k-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence, for sufficiently large fixed k in the specified sequential adjacency-matrix models.
problem_status_before: Complexity of WL refinement
rating_reason: Solid complexity result.

title: Generalized star height at most three
one_line_claim: Every regular language over a finite alphabet has a generalized regular expression with at most three nested Kleene stars, allowing union, concatenation and complement over the same alphabet.
problem_status_before: Generalized star-height problem open since the 1960s
rating_reason: An absolute bound of three is a striking answer to a classical automata question.

title: Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication
one_line_claim: Over every characteristic-zero field, the (1,1) entry of a product of n independent n× n variable matrices requires n^Theta(√ n) gates in homogeneous depth-five sum–product circuits.
problem_status_before: Arithmetic circuit lower bounds for restricted models
rating_reason: Specialist lower bound.

title: A quasilinear PCP theorem for PPAD
one_line_claim: Resolves the quasilinear PCP-for-PPAD conjecture.
problem_status_before: Recent PPAD PCP conjecture
rating_reason: Specialist complexity result.

title: One-tape time simulation in two-fifths-power space
one_line_claim: Determines the halting and finite-control outcome of a fixed deterministic one-writable-tape machine up to time T using O(T^2/5log^C(T+2)) space, improving the square-root exponent.
problem_status_before: Williams (2025) √T space simulation
rating_reason: Improves a brand-new breakthrough in a restricted model.

title: Subset Sum in O(2^0.49n) time
one_line_claim: Gives a uniform randomized classical algorithm for worst-case Subset Sum in ordinary O(2^0.49n) word-RAM time on polynomial-bit inputs, where n counts the integers.
problem_status_before: Horowitz–Sahni 2^{n/2} (1974) unbeaten in the worst case
rating_reason: Beating meet-in-the-middle for Subset Sum is a famous open problem.

title: Subpolynomial query complexity for log-concave sampling
one_line_claim: For C2 potentials with a supplied minimizer and Ipreceqnabla^2Vpreceq2I, proves that sampling within total variation 1/10 requires only C_ε d^ε exact value-and-gradient queries for every fixed ε &gt 0.
problem_status_before: Query complexity of log-concave sampling open
rating_reason: Surprising sampling result.

title: Memory–sample lower bounds for noiseless Gaussian regression
one_line_claim: For fixed A &gt 0, a one-pass learner with Ad^2 persistent bits needs Omega_A(dlog(1/epsilon)) noiseless Gaussian samples to recover a unit vector to angular error 0< epsilon≤1/10 with probability 2/3, uniformly in accuracy for large d.
problem_status_before: Memory-sample tradeoffs
rating_reason: Specialist learning-theory lower bound.

title: Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy
one_line_claim: Proves that the existential theory of the reals lies in the counting hierarchy.
problem_status_before: ETR ⊆ PSPACE (Canny 1988); CH open
rating_reason: Big upgrade on the complexity of real algebraic geometry.

title: Deterministic polynomial factorization over prime fields
one_line_claim: Gives a uniform deterministic algorithm that completely factors every nonzero dense degree-n polynomial over a prime field 𝔽p, including multiplicities, in bit complexity polynomial in (n+1)log p.
problem_status_before: Open since Berlekamp (1970); known only under GRH or for special cases
rating_reason: Deterministic polynomial factoring over F_p is a classic open problem.

title: Hilbert's sixteenth problem: uniform bounds for limit cycles
one_line_claim: Resolves the uniform boundedness assertion in Hilbert's sixteenth problem: the number of isolated periodic orbits of a real planar polynomial vector field is bounded by a finite constant depending only on its degree.
problem_status_before: Hilbert's 16th problem, second part (1900); finiteness unknown even for quadratic fields; Smale's 13th problem
rating_reason: Uniform finiteness of limit cycles would settle a Hilbert problem considered among the hardest.
verification: Lean, partial (only the quintic Liénard two-cycle bound; the uniform Hilbert-16 finiteness claim is unformalized)
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (check statement fidelity). If true, comparable in fame to a Millennium Problem. Comparator statement read by researcher6 (Lean statement is only: quintic Liénard systems have ≤ 2 limit cycles).

title: Banach’s simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem
one_line_claim: Resolves the probability-preserving form of Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem within smooth dynamics.
problem_status_before: Banach's question (Scottish Book) on simple Lebesgue spectrum
rating_reason: Answers a famous ergodic-theory question in the smooth category.

title: Rokhlin’s multiple-mixing problem
one_line_claim: Proves that every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation is mixing of all finite orders, resolving Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for a single transformation.
problem_status_before: Rokhlin (1949); known for rank-one and special classes
rating_reason: Settles a famous 75-year-old ergodic-theory problem.

title: Positive metric entropy for the standard map
one_line_claim: Proves that the standard sine map on the two-dimensional torus has positive metric entropy with respect to area for every sufficiently large positive parameter.
problem_status_before: Sinai's conjecture on positive metric entropy for the Chirikov standard map; considered one of the hardest problems in smooth dynamics
rating_reason: Would be a landmark in the theory of nonuniformly hyperbolic systems.

title: The near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture
one_line_claim: Resolves the near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture for smooth strictly convex planar billiards of positive curvature.
problem_status_before: Birkhoff conjecture; local versions by Avila–De Simoi–Kaloshin
rating_reason: Progress on a famous billiards conjecture.

title: The entropy-rate dimension formula for self-similar measures
one_line_claim: For every self-similar measure on the line generated by finitely many contracting similarities, proves dim_Hμ=min{1,h_RW/χ}, where h_RW is the entropy rate of random composed maps and χ the average logarithmic contraction.
problem_status_before: Hochman (2014) proved the formula under exponential separation; general case open
rating_reason: Removes the separation hypothesis from a central fractal-geometry conjecture.

title: Classwise permanence for weakly reversible mass-action systems
one_line_claim: Proves the permanence conjecture for every finite weakly reversible mass-action system with fixed positive rate constants.
problem_status_before: Permanence conjecture tied to Horn's Global Attractor Conjecture (1974)
rating_reason: Settles a central conjecture in chemical reaction network theory.

title: Weak mixing of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
one_line_claim: Proves that the billiard flow in every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with at least one angle irrational relative to π is weakly mixing for normalized area times uniform direction.
problem_status_before: Ergodicity of billiards in all irrational triangles open; only generic triangles (Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie)
rating_reason: Weak mixing for every irrational triangle settles a famous billiards problem.
verification: Lean, core claim formalized (ergodicity formalized; weak mixing is not)

title: A C1 counterexample to the entropy conjecture
one_line_claim: Constructs a noninvertible C1 self-map of a compact smooth manifold with zero topological entropy but eigenvalue 2 on second homology.
problem_status_before: Shub's entropy conjecture (1974); true for C^∞ (Yomdin)
rating_reason: Counterexample in C¹ settles a classic question.

title: Zero entropy does not guarantee a smooth positive-volume model
one_line_claim: Constructs a zero-entropy ergodic invertible transformation of a standard nonatomic probability space that is not measurably conjugate to any C∞ diffeomorphism preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density on a compact finite-dimensional manifold.
problem_status_before: Smooth realization problem (Kushnirenko, Anosov–Katok)
rating_reason: Answers a famous realization question.
verification: Lean, partial (finite-entropy version only; zero-entropy claim unformalized)

title: Arithmetic classification and non-Pisot singularity for Bernoulli convolutions
one_line_claim: Classifies singular and absolutely continuous unbiased Bernoulli convolutions for every λ∈(0,1) by an infinite, one-sided approximation condition using explicit finite sets of algebraic units.
problem_status_before: Erdős (1939); classification of absolutely continuous Bernoulli convolutions a famous open problem
rating_reason: A full classification would end an 85-year-old problem.

title: Pointwise multiple ergodic averages for mixing transformations
one_line_claim: Proves almost-everywhere convergence of consecutive multiple ergodic averages of every finite length for invertible mixing probability-preserving transformations.
problem_status_before: Pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages open beyond special cases (Bourgain double recurrence)
rating_reason: Strong progress on a central ergodic-theory question.

title: A counterexample to periodic tiling in dimension three
one_line_claim: Constructs a finite translational tile in ℤ3 that tiles space but admits no fully periodic tiling, disproving the periodic tiling conjecture in the smallest possible lattice dimension.
problem_status_before: Greenfeld–Tao (2022) disproved periodic tiling in high dimension; true in dimension 2
rating_reason: Sharp-dimension counterexample.

title: Borsuk's conjecture fails in dimension nine
one_line_claim: Constructs a compact subset of ℝ9 that cannot be covered by ten sets of strictly smaller diameter, disproving Borsuk's covering assertion already in dimension nine.
problem_status_before: Borsuk (1933) disproved by Kahn–Kalai (1993); smallest known counterexample dimension 64
rating_reason: Dimension 9 would be a dramatic improvement.

title: Graph coloring, clique minors, and Colin de Verdière invariants
one_line_claim: Disproves Hadwiger's conjecture even for fractional coloring: arbitrarily large finite simple graphs with independence number at most two satisfy χ_f(G)> h(G), where h(G) is the largest clique-minor order.
problem_status_before: Hadwiger's conjecture (1943), one of graph theory's most famous; fractional relaxation was believed true
rating_reason: χ_f > h disproves Hadwiger's conjecture outright; plus a linear list-coloring bound.
verification: Lean, partial (only the linear list-Hadwiger bound; the counterexample to Hadwiger (fractional) is unformalized)
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Note: refutes Hadwiger itself, a stronger claim than the title suggests.

title: The Euclidean plane cannot be colored with five colors
one_line_claim: Proves that every five-coloring of the Euclidean plane has a monochromatic pair at distance one, with no restriction on the color classes.
problem_status_before: Hadwiger–Nelson: χ ≥ 5 (de Grey 2018), ≤ 7
rating_reason: Advances a famous problem; requires handling arbitrary (non-measurable) colorings.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Comparator statement read by researcher6 (statement file read is the classical 7-coloring upper bound; the 5-color exclusion has its own file (not read)).

title: Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial Szemerédi bounds
one_line_claim: Proves Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length.
problem_status_before: Erdős–Turán conjecture ($5000 Erdős prize); quasipolynomial bounds only for k=3 (Kelley–Meka 2023)
rating_reason: Settles a famous Erdős prize problem and gives near-optimal Szemerédi bounds.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Reasoning trace released. Comparator statement read by researcher6 (divergent reciprocal sum ⇒ k-APs for every k); faithful to the claim. Called hard to read on Bluesky (exposition, not an error).

title: Superexponential van der Waerden numbers
one_line_claim: Resolves Erdős's superexponential-growth question for van der Waerden numbers.
problem_status_before: Erdős asked whether W(k)^{1/k} → ∞; best lower bounds exponential
rating_reason: A superexponential lower bound is a long-sought Ramsey result.

title: Counterexamples to Sidorenko’s conjecture and the forcing conjecture
one_line_claim: Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture with a connected bipartite pattern on 35 vertices and 66 edges that occurs less frequently than in a random graph of the same edge density.
problem_status_before: Sidorenko (1993) and Erdős–Simonovits; widely believed true
rating_reason: Disproving Sidorenko would be a major surprise in extremal graph theory.

title: Counterexamples to Ryser’s covering conjecture
one_line_claim: Disproves Ryser's covering conjecture by constructing intersecting (q+1)-partite, (q+1)-uniform hypergraphs with covering number q+1, rather than the predicted bound q, for every sufficiently large prime q.
problem_status_before: Ryser (1971); proven for r ≤ 3
rating_reason: Counterexample to a famous hypergraph conjecture.

title: Hindman’s finite sums and products conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture: every finite coloring of the positive integers contains sets of any prescribed finite size whose nonempty subset sums and nonempty subset products all have one common color.
problem_status_before: Hindman (1979); Moreira (2017) partial
rating_reason: Settles a famous Ramsey-theory conjecture.

title: The Harary–Hill and Zarankiewicz crossing-number formulas
one_line_claim: Resolves the Harary–Hill conjecture and Turán's brickyard problem in the Zarankiewicz formulation, determining the crossing numbers of every complete and complete bipartite graph.
problem_status_before: Turán's brick factory (1944), Zarankiewicz (1954), Harary–Hill (1962)
rating_reason: Settles two classic crossing-number conjectures.

title: The higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture
one_line_claim: For every fixed d ≥ 3, any n ≥ 2 distinct points in ℝd determine at least c_dn^2/d distinct distances, with c_d> 0 depending only on dimension.
problem_status_before: Erdős distinct distances in d ≥ 3 open (Guth–Katz did d = 2)
rating_reason: Higher-dimensional analogue of a celebrated result.

title: Planar distinct distances and unit-distance bounds
one_line_claim: Proves the weak pinned Erdős distance conjecture: for every fixed ε &gt 0, all but o(n) points of any n-point planar set determine at least n^1-ε distinct nonzero distances.
problem_status_before: Unit distances stuck at n^{4/3} since Spencer–Szemerédi–Trotter (1984)
rating_reason: Breaking the 4/3 barrier is a famous long-standing goal.

title: Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
one_line_claim: Resolves the full combinatorial invariance conjecture: isomorphic Bruhat intervals in arbitrary Coxeter systems have identical equal-parameter Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials.
problem_status_before: Combinatorial invariance (Lusztig, Dyer 1980s); DeepMind-assisted partial progress (2021)
rating_reason: Settles a central conjecture of algebraic combinatorics.

title: Shareshian–Wachs elementary positivity
one_line_claim: Resolves the elementary-positivity part of the Shareshian–Wachs conjecture: the chromatic quasisymmetric function of every natural unit interval graph has elementary-basis coefficients in ℕ[q].
problem_status_before: Stanley–Stembridge proved by Hikita (2024); Shareshian–Wachs q-version open
rating_reason: Natural graded strengthening of a recent breakthrough.

title: Sharp logarithmic exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
one_line_claim: For every fixed integer s ≥ 5, proves r(s,t)=t^s-1/(log t)^s-2+o(1) as t→∞, determining the logarithmic exponent and matching the classical upper bound at that scale.
problem_status_before: r(4,t) order found by Mattheus–Verstraete (2023)
rating_reason: Sharp off-diagonal Ramsey asymptotics up to log exponent.

title: The hypercube Ramsey conjecture
one_line_claim: Resolves the Burr–Erdős hypercube Ramsey conjecture: the two-color Ramsey number of the n-dimensional cube is Theta(2^n).
problem_status_before: Burr–Erdős (1970s); best bounds 2^{(2−c)n}
rating_reason: Settles a known Ramsey conjecture.

title: Classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
one_line_claim: Classifies finite point configurations that occur monochromatically, at their original scale, in every finite coloring of sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space.
problem_status_before: Euclidean Ramsey theory (Erdős–Graham et al. 1973); Graham's spherical conjecture
rating_reason: Classifying Euclidean Ramsey sets would end a major line.

title: Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture: every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many vertices at directed distance exactly two as at directed distance one.
problem_status_before: Seymour (1990), famous digraph conjecture
rating_reason: Settles a famous graph-theory conjecture.

title: Deterministic construction of strong thin spanning trees
one_line_claim: Resolves the strong thin-tree conjecture constructively.
problem_status_before: Goddyn's strong thin tree conjecture
rating_reason: Implies constant-factor ATSP via thin trees; long-standing.

title: Talagrand’s expectation thresholds, discrete convexity, and graph decompositions
one_line_claim: Proves that integral and fractional expectation thresholds differ by at most a universal factor, and resolves Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture.
problem_status_before: Talagrand's conjectures (2010)
rating_reason: Settles prize-offered Talagrand conjectures.

title: The second Kahn–Kalai conjecture with an edge-count bound
one_line_claim: Proves the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture: for every finite simple graph H with h ≥ 1 edges and at most n vertices, its appearance threshold in G(n,p) is at most C p_E(n,H)(1+log_2 h), with universal C. Here p_E is the least density at which every subgraph of H has expected copy count at least 1/2.
problem_status_before: Kahn–Kalai second conjecture
rating_reason: Natural follow-up to Park–Pham.

title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders
one_line_claim: Constructs arbitrarily large finite d-dimensional simplicial complexes, for every d ≥ 3, with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform 𝔽2 coboundary expansion in every degree below d.
problem_status_before: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in dimension ≥3 open
rating_reason: Important for high-dimensional expansion and codes.

title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree
one_line_claim: For every fixed d ≥ 3, constructs a simple d-regular nonbipartite Ramanujan graph on every sufficiently large even number n of vertices, with every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue strictly between -2√d-1 and 2√d-1.
problem_status_before: Existence of nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs of all degrees known probabilistically (Huang–McKenzie–Yau 2024); deterministic construction open
rating_reason: Explicit Ramanujan graphs for all degrees.

title: The circulant Hadamard and Barker-sequence conjectures
one_line_claim: Proves that real circulant Hadamard matrices exist exactly in orders 1 and 4, resolving the circulant Hadamard conjecture.
problem_status_before: Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture (1963); Barker sequences
rating_reason: Settles a famous combinatorial-design conjecture.

title: Barnette’s Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves that every finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-vertex-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, resolving Barnette's conjecture.
problem_status_before: Barnette (1969)
rating_reason: Settles a famous Hamiltonicity conjecture.

title: The Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves that the edges of every finite simple undirected graph on n vertices can be partitioned into at most Cn simple cycles and single edges, for an absolute constant C. This resolves the Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture, bounding the number of pieces linearly even for dense graphs.
problem_status_before: Erdős–Gallai (1966); O(n log* n) by Bucić–Montgomery (2022)
rating_reason: Settles a classic decomposition conjecture.

title: Power savings for intersective polynomial differences and prime arguments
