one_line_claim: For every fixed intersective integer polynomial h of degree k ≥ 2 with positive leading coefficient, proves that a subset of {1,…,N} avoiding nonzero values h(1),h(2),… as differences has size O_h(N^1-c_k), with c_k> 0 depending only on degree.
problem_status_before: Sárközy-type problems; power savings known only in special cases
rating_reason: Strong quantitative additive combinatorics.

title: Power savings for planar halving lines and k-sets
one_line_claim: Improves the planar halving-line bound to O(n^4/3-ε) for sets with no three collinear and an absolute ε &gt 0.
problem_status_before: Dey's n^{4/3} (1998) halving-line bound unbeaten
rating_reason: Breaking Dey's bound is a famous combinatorial-geometry goal.

title: Correspondence coloring with a fixed forbidden subgraph
one_line_claim: Proves the Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov coloring conjecture in correspondence-coloring form: graphs avoiding any fixed subgraph F need O_F(Δ/logΔ) colors when their maximum degree Δ is sufficiently large.
problem_status_before: Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov and Ajtai–Erdős–Komlós–Szemerédi conjectures
rating_reason: Settles two known graph-coloring conjectures.

title: Counterexamples to infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering
one_line_claim: Disproves the unrestricted infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering conjectures in ZFC, using two self-dual partitional matroids on a countably infinite ground set.
problem_status_before: Infinite matroid intersection conjecture (Nash-Williams variant)
rating_reason: Answers a known infinite-combinatorics question negatively.

title: Uniform influence and sharp thresholds for graph and hypergraph properties
one_line_claim: Proves the Friedgut–Kalai threshold-width conjectures for graphs and fixed-uniformity hypergraphs.
problem_status_before: Friedgut–Kalai (1996) threshold-width conjectures
rating_reason: Settles classical sharp-threshold conjectures.

title: Snaky in 21 Maker moves
one_line_claim: Settles the Snaky achievement problem: Maker can force the six-cell Snaky shape within 21 of its own moves on the initially empty infinite square board.
problem_status_before: Harary's achievement games; Snaky the one open case
rating_reason: A beloved puzzle, little mathematical consequence.

title: The sharp terminal leave in random triangle removal
one_line_claim: Starting from the complete graph on n vertices, repeatedly delete a uniformly chosen remaining triangle.
problem_status_before: Bohman–Frieze–Lubetzky proved n^{3/2+o(1)}
rating_reason: Sharp constant in a known random process.

title: Cycle–clique Ramsey numbers
one_line_claim: Proves the Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture: R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1 for every m≥ n≥3, except R(C_3,K_3)=6.
problem_status_before: Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp (1978)
rating_reason: Settles a classic Ramsey-number conjecture.

title: Polynomial removal fails for ordered binary matrices
one_line_claim: Disproves polynomial ordered binary matrix removal with one fixed 66×66 zero–one pattern.
problem_status_before: Ordered matrix removal
rating_reason: Niche counterexample.

title: A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound
one_line_claim: For every sufficiently large n, constructs n points in the unit square such that every triangle has area at least n^-2+c for one absolute c &gt 0.
problem_status_before: Heilbronn triangle problem; Komlós–Pintz–Szemerédi lower bound n^{-2} log n
rating_reason: Disproves a conjectured bound in a classic problem.

title: Boolean functions violate the square-root degree bound by arbitrary factors
one_line_claim: Disproves the proposed square-root bound relating a Boolean function's linear Fourier coefficients to its polynomial degree.
problem_status_before: Proposed Fourier-degree bound
rating_reason: Niche counterexample in Boolean analysis.

title: Serre’s intersection-multiplicity conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves strict positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity χ^R(M,N) for nonzero finitely generated modules over any regular local ring, provided Motimes_R N has finite length and dim M+dim N=dim R. This resolves the positivity conjecture, including ramified mixed characteristic.
problem_status_before: Serre (1961); positivity open in ramified mixed characteristic
rating_reason: Settles Serre's last open multiplicity conjecture.

title: Lech’s multiplicity conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves e(R)≤ e(S) for every flat local homomorphism of nonzero Noetherian local rings, where e is Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity.
problem_status_before: Lech (1960), famous in commutative algebra
rating_reason: Settles a 65-year-old conjecture.
verification: Lean, partial (only a supporting Dutta-multiplicity comparison; Lech's conjecture itself is unformalized)

title: A counterexample to the small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture
one_line_claim: Constructs a three-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain over ℂ with no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module.
problem_status_before: Hochster's small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture
rating_reason: A counterexample would overturn a central expectation of commutative algebra.

title: A counterexample to Kaplansky’s zero-divisor conjecture
one_line_claim: Constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group G whose group algebra 𝔽_2[G] has nonzero zero divisors, disproving Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture.
problem_status_before: Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture (1950s); Gardam (2021) disproved the stronger unit conjecture
rating_reason: Disproves a famous group-ring conjecture that survived the unit-conjecture counterexample.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Comparator statement read by researcher6 (finitely presented torsion-free G with zero divisors in F_2[G]); faithful to the claim.

title: A torsion-free group algebra that is not directly finite
one_line_claim: Constructs a finitely presented torsion-free nonsofic group whose group algebra over 𝔽2 is not directly finite, disproving Kaplansky's conjecture even without torsion.
problem_status_before: Direct finiteness known for sofic groups; whether every group is sofic, and Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture (1973), are famous open problems
rating_reason: A non-surjunctive (hence nonsofic) group would answer one of the biggest open questions in group theory and dynamics, plus disprove the Determinant Conjecture.
verification: Lean, core claim formalized (direct-finiteness counterexample (group with torsion) and determinant counterexample formalized; torsion-free and nonsofic claims are not)
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Reasoning trace released. Claims the first nonsofic group, a much bigger claim than the title suggests. Comparator statement read by researcher6 (ab = 1, ba ≠ 1 in K[G], char 2, finitely presented G with odd torsion); faithful to the claim.

title: A counterexample to finitistic-dimension finiteness
one_line_claim: Constructs a finite-dimensional complex algebra whose finite-dimensional modules have unbounded finite projective dimensions.
problem_status_before: Little finitistic dimension conjecture (Bass 1960), central in representation theory of algebras
rating_reason: Disproof overturns a central homological conjecture.

title: Counterexamples to Auslander–Reiten, Tachikawa and related homological conjectures
one_line_claim: Constructs finite-dimensional algebras over a characteristic-two rational-function field that disprove the Auslander–Reiten and Gorenstein-projective conjectures, and Tachikawa's second conjecture.
problem_status_before: Nakayama (1958), Auslander–Reiten, Tachikawa conjectures, central to representation theory of algebras
rating_reason: Disproving the Nakayama and Auslander–Reiten conjectures would upend a classical program.
verification: Lean, core claim formalized (Auslander–Reiten and Tachikawa counterexamples formalized; Nakayama-type consequences are not)
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Examples over a non-algebraically-closed char-2 field.

title: Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers
one_line_claim: Proves the Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers conjectures over every characteristic-zero field.
problem_status_before: Eisenbud–Green–Harris (1993)
rating_reason: Settles a famous commutative-algebra conjecture in char 0.

title: A counterexample to Kurosh’s division-ring problem
one_line_claim: Constructs a countable characteristic-zero division ring that is algebraic over its center and generated by two elements over that center, but has infinite dimension over it.
problem_status_before: Kurosh (1941) problem for division rings
rating_reason: Negative answer to a classical ring-theory problem.

title: The blockwise Alperin weight conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves the numerical blockwise Alperin weight conjecture for every prime and every finite group: the number of irreducible Brauer characters in a block equals the number of conjugacy classes of its weights.
problem_status_before: Alperin weight conjecture (1986), one of the main conjectures of modular representation theory; McKay proved 2024
rating_reason: Proving it for all finite groups would be a landmark in group representation theory.

title: Donovan's conjecture over fields and complete mixed-characteristic DVRs
one_line_claim: Proves Donovan's conjecture: over each fixed algebraically closed field of characteristic p, blocks of finite groups with bounded defect-group order have only finitely many Morita-equivalence classes, for every prime p.
problem_status_before: Donovan's conjecture (1970s); reductions by Eaton–Livesey
rating_reason: Settles a central finiteness conjecture in block theory.

title: Tensor saturation for even spin groups
one_line_claim: Proves saturation factor one for mathopSpinnolimits (2n), n ≥ 2: for three dominant integral weights whose sum lies in the root lattice, an invariant at any common positive integral dilation already gives an invariant at the original weights.
problem_status_before: Saturation conjecture (Kapovich–Millson) type D
rating_reason: Specialist Lie-theory result.

title: Saxl’s conjecture and universal tensor squares
one_line_claim: Proves Saxl's conjecture: the tensor square of every staircase representation contains every irreducible complex representation of the corresponding symmetric group.
problem_status_before: Saxl (2012)
rating_reason: Settles a popular symmetric-group conjecture.

title: Finite lattice representation and undecidability
one_line_claim: Some finite lattices are not congruence lattices of any finite algebra, answering the finite lattice representation problem negatively.
problem_status_before: Finite lattice representation problem (Pálfy–Pudlák 1980), famous in universal algebra
rating_reason: Negative answer plus undecidability settles a 45-year-old problem.
verification: Lean, partial (only the graph characterization; nonrepresentability and undecidability are unformalized)

title: The ℓ¹-Bass conjecture for all discrete groups
one_line_claim: Proves the ℓ1-Bass conjecture for every discrete group: Hattori–Stallings traces of idempotent matrices over ell^1(G) are supported on finitely many finite-order conjugacy classes.
problem_status_before: Bass conjecture (1976); Kaplansky idempotent conjecture open for general torsion-free groups
rating_reason: Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture for torsion-free groups in char 0 is a famous problem.

title: Finite symmetric tensor categories and the Verlinde tower
one_line_claim: Proves that every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p &gt 0 admits a k-linear exact faithful strong symmetric monoidal fiber functor to a higher Verlinde category Ver_p^n.
problem_status_before: Benson–Etingof–Ostrik conjecture
rating_reason: Positive-characteristic Deligne-type theorem.

title: Integral counterexamples to Gersten’s conjecture
one_line_claim: Disproves unrestricted integral Gersten injectivity in degrees 3 and 5.
problem_status_before: Gersten's conjecture (1973); open in mixed characteristic
rating_reason: Integral counterexamples in mixed characteristic.

title: Foulkes' conjecture for sixth powers and quadratic stabilization
one_line_claim: Proves the sixth case of Foulkes’ conjecture: mathopSymnolimits ^6(mathopSymnolimits ^bV) embeds equivariantly in mathopSymnolimits ^b(mathopSymnolimits ^6V) for every b ≥ 6 and finite-dimensional complex V. More generally, the canonical multiplication map mathopSymnolimits ^b(mathopSymnolimits ^aV)→mathopSymnolimits ^a(mathopSymnolimits ^bV) is surjective for a ≥ 2 and b≥ a(a-1), giving dimens…
problem_status_before: Foulkes' conjecture (1950); small cases known
rating_reason: One more case of a classical plethysm conjecture.

title: The geometric phase diagram, diffusion, and spectra of random planar maps
one_line_claim: Critical Fortuin–Kasteleyn planar maps converge to Liouville quantum gravity spheres for 0< q≤4 and to the Brownian continuum random tree for q &gt 4, establishing the surface-to-tree geometric transition.
problem_status_before: Sheffield's FK-map/LQG program; random walk on maps to Liouville Brownian motion open
rating_reason: Convergence of FK planar maps to LQG would be a major probability result.
verification: Lean, partial (only the q > 4 tree limit; the LQG limits for q ≤ 4 are unformalized)
notable_flags: Lean-formalized but conditional on stated Brownian/LQG inputs; check scope.

title: Planar first-passage geometry and the absence of bigeodesics
one_line_claim: Proves that planar first-passage percolation has no doubly infinite geodesic for iid nonnegative nonatomic edge weights when the minimum of four weights has finite second moment.
problem_status_before: Bigeodesics question (Furstenberg/Kesten/Newman); strict convexity of FPP limit shape open
rating_reason: Settles two famous first-passage-percolation problems.
verification: Lean, partial (only limit-shape differentiability; no-bigeodesics and strict convexity are unformalized)

title: Critical percolation on every quasi-transitive graph
one_line_claim: Resolves the Benjamini–Schramm criticality conjecture for bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with p_c< 1: at the critical probability, there is almost surely no infinite cluster.
problem_status_before: Continuity at p_c on Z³ is one of the most famous open problems in probability; Benjamini–Schramm conjecture (1996)
rating_reason: No percolation at criticality on Z³ and all quasi-transitive graphs would be a field-changing result.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (check statement fidelity). Comparator statement read by researcher6 (no infinite cluster at p_c for bond and site percolation on Z³); faithful to the claim.

title: The Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture
one_line_claim: Proves p_c< p_u for Bernoulli bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite nonamenable quasi-transitive graph, resolving the Benjamini–Schramm nonuniqueness conjecture.
problem_status_before: Benjamini–Schramm p_c < p_u (1996); Hutchcroft partial
rating_reason: Settles a central conjecture of percolation beyond Z^d.

title: Canonical O(3) continuum limit and exact O(4) mass asymptotics
one_line_claim: Constructs the canonical continuum limit of the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor O(3) model: a non-Gaussian local relativistic theory with a unique vacuum and a positive mass gap.
problem_status_before: Polyakov's prediction of a mass gap for 2D O(n≥3) models at all temperatures; continuum O(3) σ-model unconstructed
rating_reason: A rigorous asymptotically-free theory with mass gap is a famous toy version of the Yang–Mills problem.
verification: Lean, core claim formalized (2D O(n≥3) exponential decay formalized; continuum O(3) and O(4) gap are not)
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (check scope). Comparator statement read by researcher6 (uniform exponential decay for 2D O(n≥3) at every β); faithful to the claim.

title: Critical and near-critical XY scaling and BKT universality
one_line_claim: For the square-lattice nearest-neighbor cosine XY model, proves critical axis correlations C_β_c(r)sim Ar^-1/4(log r)^1/8 and the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless essential singularity √β_c-βlogxi(β)→ B, with A,B> 0 after the free-box thermodynamic limit.
problem_status_before: Fröhlich–Spencer (1981) proved the BKT transition; exact critical behaviour open
rating_reason: Sharp BKT asymptotics are famous predictions.
notable_flags: Unformalized; some conclusions keep stated assumptions.

title: The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation law
one_line_claim: For every fixed inverse temperature β &gt 1, determines the fluctuation scale and limiting law of the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick log partition function.
problem_status_before: Predicted n^{1/6} fluctuations in low-temperature SK
rating_reason: Solid spin-glass result.

title: Conformal universality for weakly interacting and random-bond Ising models
one_line_claim: Weak finite-range square-symmetric even multispin perturbations of the square-lattice Ising model preserve critical bulk spin and energy limits weak square-symmetric contour interactions also yield chordal SLE3 interface limits.
problem_status_before: Universality of critical Ising (Smirnov's program)
rating_reason: Extends conformal invariance to perturbed and disordered models.

title: GOE bulk universality for regular graphs with weak Anderson disorder
one_line_claim: For every fixed degree d ≥ 3, the bulk adjacency-eigenvalue point process of a uniform simple random d-regular graph converges to the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble law, including for cubic graphs.
problem_status_before: Bulk universality for fixed-degree random regular graphs open
rating_reason: Major random-matrix universality result.

title: Directional zero–one laws beyond iid environments and iid ballisticity
one_line_claim: On ℤd, d ≥ 3, directional escape has probability zero or one for iid strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor environments, and for stationary ergodic finite-range-dependent environments under uniform ellipticity.
problem_status_before: Kalikow zero-one law and Sznitman's ballisticity conjecture
rating_reason: Settles central RWRE conjectures.

title: The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses
one_line_claim: Proves the Mézard–Parisi hierarchical cavity formula for Poisson-diluted even-arity Ising models satisfying the Panchenko–Talagrand factorization and positivity assumptions, with only first-moment integrability.
problem_status_before: Mézard–Parisi cavity formula; Panchenko proved it under assumptions
rating_reason: Important rigorous spin-glass result, under the stated factorization assumptions.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Reasoning trace released. Conditional on Panchenko–Talagrand assumptions.

title: Perceptron free energies and microscopic jamming exponents
one_line_claim: Determines finite-temperature variational free energies for Gaussian Ising perceptrons with bounded Borel log-potentials and Gaussian spherical perceptrons with bounded continuous potentials, at every positive pattern density.
problem_status_before: Perceptron free energy (Gardner) predictions
rating_reason: Solid rigorous statistical physics.

title: Random-cluster interfaces: critical, disordered, thermal, and natural-time scaling
one_line_claim: Proves chordal SLEκ limits for critical square-lattice random-cluster interfaces for 0< q≤4, with κ=4π/arccos(-√ q/2): bounded Jordan domains are allowed for q ≥ 1, and smooth Jordan domains for q &lt 1, under the stated marked-boundary approximations.
problem_status_before: Conformal invariance of FK interfaces known only for q = 2 (Smirnov); square-lattice bond percolation (q = 1) open
rating_reason: SLE limits for all 0 < q ≤ 4, including critical bond percolation on Z², would be a landmark.

title: Critical and quenched near-critical universality for Poisson–Voronoi percolation
one_line_claim: Proves Cardy's formula for annealed critical Poisson–Voronoi crossing probabilities in every bounded Jordan quadrilateral.
problem_status_before: Voronoi percolation conformal invariance open
rating_reason: Universality result for a natural model.

title: Gaussian free field limits throughout the balanced six-vertex regime
one_line_claim: The balanced square-lattice six-vertex height field with a=b=1 and 0< c≤2 converges to a Gaussian free field, including at the endpoint c = 2.
problem_status_before: Six-vertex GFF convergence known in parts of the regime
rating_reason: Settles a well-known 2D statistical-mechanics conjecture.

title: The double-dimer loop ensemble converges to CLE4
one_line_claim: Resolves the half-plane Temperleyan form of the double-dimer scaling-limit conjecture: the complete loop ensemble formed by two independent dimer coverings of the Temperleyan square lattice converges to nested CLE4.
problem_status_before: Kenyon's double-dimer CLE4 conjecture
rating_reason: Settles a known scaling-limit conjecture.

title: Critical SK autocorrelation processes and dynamics across the temperature transition
one_line_claim: For zero-field Gaussian SK heat-bath dynamics with rate-one updates per spin, proves worst-start cutoff on the log n scale for fixed 0≤β< 1, mixing time n^2/3+o(1) at β = 1, and stretched-exponential mixing from a Gibbs-sampled fixed starting configuration for β &gt 1, in probability over disorder.
problem_status_before: SK Glauber dynamics mixing
rating_reason: Solid dynamics result.

title: Continuum phase transitions for radial pair potentials
one_line_claim: Constructs stable distance-dependent pair interactions for three-dimensional classical particles with a first-order phase transition: the canonical free energy has a derivative jump at one inverse temperature throughout an open density interval.
problem_status_before: Proving a phase transition for continuum particles with a pure pair potential is a famous open problem (Simon)
rating_reason: Answers a long-standing statistical-mechanics challenge.

title: Exact three- and four-state reconstruction thresholds and four-state tree capacity
one_line_claim: Proves the exact reconstruction threshold dλ^2> 1, with nonreconstruction at equality, for three-state symmetric and four-state ferromagnetic broadcasting on regular trees (d ≥ 2) and observed Poisson trees (mean d &gt 1 and d &gt 0, respectively), with Poisson advantage averaged without conditioning on survival.
problem_status_before: Kesten–Stigum tightness for few states
rating_reason: Solid reconstruction result.

title: Exact Hausdorff gauges for SLE
one_line_claim: Resolves Schramm’s Hausdorff-measure question for chordal SLEκ, 0< κ< 8.
problem_status_before: Schramm's question on SLE gauge
rating_reason: Fine-grained SLE geometry.

title: The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID
one_line_claim: On every infinite connected locally finite simple unweighted graph, the free uniform spanning forest is a factor of independent vertex labels, by one isomorphism-equivariant rule using no root.
problem_status_before: Lyons's factor-of-IID questions
rating_reason: Solid probability result.

title: Gaussian fields and interfaces for triangular-lattice Lipschitz heights
one_line_claim: Proves Gaussian free field limits on bounded smooth simply connected domains for triangular-lattice height models: uniform odd heights with increments 0,pm2 and two-arc boundary values pm1, and zero-boundary integer Lipschitz heights weighted by fixed x∈[1/√2,1].
problem_status_before: Height-function GFF conjectures
rating_reason: Solid 2D statistical mechanics.

title: The joint critical Ashkin–Teller current limit
one_line_claim: Identifies the joint scaling limit of Ashkin–Teller heights and both complete current-cluster collections throughout the critical line, including the four-state Potts endpoint.
problem_status_before: Ashkin–Teller scaling limits
rating_reason: Specialist scaling limit.

title: All-temperature pressure of orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses
one_line_claim: Gives an exact variational formula for the limiting pressure of orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses at every fixed temperature, both almost surely and in expectation.
problem_status_before: Orthogonally invariant spin glasses (Marinari–Parisi–Ritort)
rating_reason: Solid spin-glass result.

title: Limiting random SAT thresholds, sharp variance and computability
one_line_claim: For random k-SAT with independent uniformly signed proper clauses sampled with replacement, proves finite positive limiting thresholds and hitting-time variance Theta_k(n) for every fixed k ≥ 3, and computability of the 3-SAT threshold.
problem_status_before: Satisfiability threshold conjecture; proved for large k (Ding–Sly–Sun 2015), open for k = 3
rating_reason: Threshold existence for every k ≥ 3 settles a famous conjecture.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Priority credited to Gaia Carenini's concurrent ECCC TR26-229 (public 5 Oct 2026).

title: The exact factor-of-IID threshold for free Ising spins on trees
one_line_claim: Determines when the free zero-field ferromagnetic Ising state on the infinite d-regular tree is a factor of independent vertex labels: exactly when tanhβ≤(d-1)^-1/2, including equality, for d ≥ 3 and β ≥ 0.
problem_status_before: Lyons's question on Ising factors of IID
rating_reason: Specialist result.

title: The three-quarter exponent for honeycomb self-avoiding walk
one_line_claim: Proves the diameter form of Nienhuis's predicted three-quarter exponent: a uniformly chosen n-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice has diameter n^3/4+o(1).
problem_status_before: Nienhuis's ν = 3/4 prediction (1982); only the connective constant is proven (Duminil-Copin–Smirnov 2010)
rating_reason: A rigorous 3/4 exponent for 2D self-avoiding walk would be a celebrated breakthrough.
verification: Lean, partial (only supporting summability and free-energy statements; the 3/4 exponent is unformalized)

title: Optimal logarithmic mixing of the Thorp shuffle
one_line_claim: Proves that the Thorp shuffle randomizes N=2^d labeled cards in Theta(log N) physical shuffles, settling its optimal mixing order for power-of-two deck sizes.
problem_status_before: Thorp shuffle; Morris proved polylog bounds
rating_reason: Settles optimal mixing order.

title: Sharp singularity rates for symmetric random sign matrices
one_line_claim: Determines the sharp exponential singularity rate of symmetric random sign matrices with independent entries on and above the diagonal.
problem_status_before: Vershynin's question; exponential bounds by Campos et al.
rating_reason: Sharp singularity rate for symmetric sign matrices.

title: Shelah's eventual categoricity and the prescribed-threshold obstruction
one_line_claim: Proves Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in ZFC: for each bound on the Löwenheim–Skolem number, a uniform threshold makes categoricity of an abstract elementary class in one cardinal above that threshold imply categoricity throughout the same tail.
problem_status_before: Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for AECs, the main test problem of non-elementary classification theory
rating_reason: A ZFC proof would be a major model-theory result.
verification: Lean, partial (only the CH obstruction; the eventual categoricity theorem is unformalized)

title: Rigidity of the Turing degrees
one_line_claim: Every order automorphism of the Turing degrees is the identity, resolving their rigidity problem.
problem_status_before: Rigidity of the Turing degrees, open since the 1960s (Slaman–Woodin partial)
rating_reason: Settles a famous computability-theory problem.

title: Single-fold Diophantine representations and undecidability under an at-most-one-solution promise
one_line_claim: Every recursively enumerable set of tuples of natural numbers has a Diophantine representation with exactly one auxiliary solution for each member and none for nonmembers.
problem_status_before: Matiyasevich's single-fold conjecture
rating_reason: Major strengthening of the Hilbert's-tenth undecidability theorem.

title: Separating choiceless counting from polynomial time and witnessed choice
one_line_claim: Confirms the Blass–Gurevich–Shelah noncapture conjecture: consistency of a linear system over 𝔽3 defines a polynomial-time query on unordered finite structures that choiceless polynomial time with counting cannot express.
problem_status_before: Blass–Gurevich–Shelah noncapture conjecture
rating_reason: Key result in descriptive complexity.

title: The Partition Principle does not imply Choice
one_line_claim: Assuming ZF is consistent, constructs a model in which every surjective image of a set injects into that set, yet the axiom of choice fails.
problem_status_before: Whether the Partition Principle implies Choice, often called the oldest open problem in set theory
rating_reason: Settles a century-old set-theory question.

title: Weak normalization implies strong normalization in pure type systems
one_line_claim: Proves that weak normalization implies strong normalization for every pure type system: if every legal expression in every valid context has a β-normal form, every β-reduction sequence terminates.
problem_status_before: Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop conjecture
rating_reason: Settles a famous type-theory conjecture.

title: Cannon's conjecture
one_line_claim: Every word-hyperbolic group with boundary homeomorphic to S2 admits a proper cocompact isometric action on hyperbolic three-space with finite kernel, proving Cannon's conjecture.
problem_status_before: Cannon's conjecture (1980s), central in geometric group theory and 3-manifolds
rating_reason: Would characterize hyperbolic 3-manifold groups by their boundary.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (extraordinary if the statement is faithful; check scope). Comparator statement read by researcher6 (hyperbolic group with S² ray-boundary acts properly cocompactly on H³ with finite kernel); faithful to the claim.

title: An infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group and a finitely presented nil algebra
one_line_claim: Constructs an infinite finitely presented residually finite group whose elements all have finite 2-power order, answering the finitely presented Burnside problem negatively even in this class.
problem_status_before: Whether a finitely presented infinite torsion group exists is a famous open problem
rating_reason: An infinite finitely presented torsion group would be a landmark.

title: Thompson's group F is nonamenable
one_line_claim: Proves that Thompson's group F, the group of dyadic piecewise linear homeomorphisms of the interval, is nonamenable, resolving its longstanding amenability problem.
problem_status_before: Amenability of Thompson's F (1970s), notorious with several retracted proofs both ways
rating_reason: Settles one of the most famous problems in group theory.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized (history of failed proofs makes formal verification decisive). Comparator statement read by researcher6 (no left-invariant mean on ℓ∞(F) for dyadic PL F); faithful to the claim.

title: A finitely generated Eilenberg–Ganea counterexample
one_line_claim: Constructs a finitely generated residually finite group with integral cohomological dimension two and geometric dimension three, disproving the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture.
problem_status_before: Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture (1957); Bestvina–Brady showed it or Whitehead's fails
rating_reason: Disproves a classical topology conjecture.

title: Boone–Higman embeddings with higher finiteness
one_line_claim: A finitely generated group has decidable word problem exactly when it embeds in a finitely presented simple group, proving the Boone–Higman conjecture.
problem_status_before: Boone–Higman (1974); hyperbolic groups by Belk et al. (2023)
rating_reason: Settles a famous decision-problem conjecture.

title: Amenability, unitarizability, and strong Ulam stability
one_line_claim: Resolves Dixmier's problem for all discrete groups: amenability is equivalent to every uniformly bounded Hilbert-space representation being similar to a unitary representation.
problem_status_before: Dixmier's unitarizability problem (1950)
rating_reason: Settles a 75-year-old problem.

title: A torsion-free hyperbolic group that is neither residually finite nor linear over any field
one_line_claim: Constructs a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite, answering the residual-finiteness question negatively.
problem_status_before: Whether every hyperbolic group is residually finite is a central open problem
rating_reason: A non-residually-finite hyperbolic group would reshape geometric group theory.
notable_flags: Lean-formalized. Comparator statement read by researcher6 (torsion-free hyperbolic, not residually finite); faithful to the claim.

title: An infinite finitely presented simple amenable group
one_line_claim: Constructs an infinite finitely presented simple amenable group, answering the longstanding question of whether these properties can occur simultaneously.
problem_status_before: Finitely presented infinite simple amenable groups open (Juschenko–Monod did finitely generated)
rating_reason: Answers a well-known question.

title: Classifying spaces and geometric obstructions for Artin groups
one_line_claim: The Salvetti complex of every finite-rank Artin group is aspherical, proving the Artin K(π,1) conjecture.
problem_status_before: Artin K(π,1) conjecture (Arnold–Brieskorn–Pham–Thom); affine case 2021
rating_reason: Settles the central conjecture on Artin groups.

title: Quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups
one_line_claim: Proves that every finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group is virtually polycyclic, resolving the Eskin–Fisher–Whyte lattice-recognition conjecture.
problem_status_before: Eskin–Fisher–Whyte conjecture
rating_reason: Major quasi-isometric rigidity result.

title: Nonsingular systems of equations over arbitrary groups
one_line_claim: Proves that every finite system of equations over an arbitrary group whose exponent-sum matrix has full row rank over ℚ has a simultaneous solution in an overgroup, resolving Howie's conjecture.
problem_status_before: Kervaire–Laudenbach conjecture (1960s); Klyachko torsion-free case
rating_reason: Settles a famous combinatorial group theory conjecture.

title: A hyperbolic group without a geometric CAT(0) action
one_line_claim: Answers negatively whether every word-hyperbolic group is a CAT(0) group.
problem_status_before: Gromov's question whether hyperbolic groups are CAT(0)
rating_reason: Answers a famous question negatively.
verification: Lean, core claim formalized (main non-CAT(0) statement formalized; dimension claims not)

title: Gersten’s conjecture and virtual compact specialness of one-relator groups
one_line_claim: Proves Gersten's conjecture: every finitely generated one-relator group containing no Baumslag–Solitar subgroup BS(m,n), with m,n≠0, is word-hyperbolic.
problem_status_before: Gersten's conjecture on one-relator groups
rating_reason: Settles a known conjecture.

title: A group without fixed price
one_line_claim: Constructs a finitely generated group with two essentially free probability-measure-preserving actions of different costs, answering the general fixed-price problem negatively.
problem_status_before: Gaboriau's fixed price problem
rating_reason: Answers the central problem of measured group theory negatively.

title: Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, rotation, and anti-de Sitter extensions
one_line_claim: Proves the sharp enclosing-area spacetime Penrose inequality for smooth one-ended asymptotically flat initial data in every spatial dimension n ≥ 3, under dominant energy, weak future trapping, positive enclosing area, and the stated decay assumptions.
problem_status_before: Penrose inequality (1973); Riemannian case by Huisken–Ilmanen and Bray
rating_reason: Spacetime version is a famous open problem in GR.
verification: Lean, partial (only supporting constructions; the spacetime Penrose inequality is unformalized)

title: Localization and delocalization in the Anderson model
one_line_claim: Resolves the predicted spectral contrast for the lattice Anderson model with independent uniform site potentials.
problem_status_before: Extended-states conjecture (3D delocalization) and 2D localization for all disorder are top open problems in random Schrödinger operators
rating_reason: Would settle the central question of Anderson localization theory.
verification: Lean, partial (only the spectrum as a set; localization and delocalization are unformalized)

title: Sharp finite-matrix Lieb–Thirring inequalities and all equality cases
one_line_claim: Proves the sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring inequality for 1/2< gamma< 3/2 and arbitrary finite-matrix potentials W ≥ 0 with ∈tmathoptrnolimits (W^gamma+1/2)< ∞: the optimal constant is the scalar one-bound-state value, independent of matrix size.
problem_status_before: Lieb–Thirring conjecture for 1/2 < γ < 3/2 in 1D
rating_reason: Settles a well-known sharp-constant conjecture.

title: The ionization and generalized ionization conjectures
one_line_claim: For the full nonrelativistic Coulomb model with two electron spin states, proves that a molecule with M fixed nuclei of charges at least one and total charge Z strictly binds at most Z+CM electrons.
problem_status_before: Ionization conjecture; Lieb's 2Z+1 bound (1984)
rating_reason: A famous mathematical-physics conjecture.
verification: Lean, partial (only ionization-energy and radius asymptotics; the Z + CM bound is unformalized)

title: Strong cosmic censorship near two-ended Kerr data
one_line_claim: Proves local strong cosmic censorship near each fixed rotating subextremal Kerr bridge.
problem_status_before: Christodoulou's strong cosmic censorship; Dafermos–Luk C⁰ stability
rating_reason: Major result in mathematical GR.

title: Area laws and tensor networks for two-dimensional gapped systems
one_line_claim: Proves an entropy area law for unique ground states of finite-range Hamiltonians on arbitrary finite induced square-lattice domains, using only a uniform full-system spectral gap and bounds on the local interactions.
problem_status_before: 2D area law for gapped systems, a central open problem in quantum information
rating_reason: Would extend Hastings' 1D theorem to 2D.

title: Exactly three mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
one_line_claim: Proves N(6)=3, resolving Zauner's dimension-six mutually unbiased bases conjecture: three such bases exist in ℂ6, but four cannot.
problem_status_before: Zauner's conjecture N(6) = 3
rating_reason: Settles a famous quantum-information problem by certified computation.

notable_flags: Lean-formalized but relies on binary64 arithmetic and compiler assumptions.

title: Positive-temperature Bose–Einstein condensation and exact quantum depletion
one_line_claim: Proves Bose–Einstein condensation for the exact canonical Gibbs state of the three-dimensional hard-sphere gas: each fixed exclusion distance and sufficiently small fixed density admit a strictly positive temperature, independent of volume, with positive condensate fraction in the thermodynamic limit.
problem_status_before: BEC for an interacting gas at positive temperature, a top open problem in mathematical physics
rating_reason: Proving BEC for hard spheres would be a historic result.
verification: Lean, core claim formalized (ground-state BEC formalized; positive-temperature BEC is unformalized)

title: The spin-one Haldane gap
one_line_claim: Proves the spin-one Haldane gap conjecture for the pure antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain on even periodic rings: the spectral gap stays uniformly positive as the chain grows.
problem_status_before: Haldane conjecture (1983) for the spin-1 Heisenberg chain
rating_reason: A rigorous Haldane gap is a famous mathematical-physics problem.

title: Uniform Laughlin gap and stability under bounded scalar disorder
one_line_claim: Proves the fermionic Laughlin spectral-gap conjecture for the full V1 interaction at filling 1/3 on the round sphere.
problem_status_before: Laughlin spectral gap conjecture
rating_reason: Rigorous foundation for the fractional quantum Hall effect.

title: Threshold and positive-energy bound states of the BFSS matrix model
one_line_claim: Proves that the undeformed relative SU(N) BFSS model has exactly one normalizable zero-energy state for every finite N ≥ 2, resolving the threshold-bound-state conjecture.
problem_status_before: BFSS threshold bound-state conjecture (Sethi–Stern N=2)
rating_reason: Important for M-theory; the SU(2) positive-energy bound states contradict the original BFSS claim.

title: Bloch's law, its lattice correction, and the spherical magnetization law
one_line_claim: Proves Bloch's T3/2 law with its exact coefficient for three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnets at every positive quantum spin, allowing nonnegative symmetric finite-range couplings whose support generates ℤ3.
problem_status_before: Spontaneous magnetization of the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet in d ≥ 3, a famous problem with no reflection positivity
rating_reason: Would settle a celebrated open problem in quantum statistical mechanics.

title: Entanglement without distillable secret key
one_line_claim: Constructs an entangled state on ℂ^10otimesℂ^10 with zero distillable secret key for the specified local-instrument protocols that complete almost surely.
problem_status_before: Christandl's PPT-square conjecture
rating_reason: Answers known quantum-information questions.

title: The entropy photon-number inequality
one_line_claim: Proves the entropy photon-number inequality for beam-splitter mixing of two independent finite-energy bosonic inputs in any finite number of modes: the output's entropy photon number is at least the transmissivity-weighted average of the inputs'. Arbitrary entanglement within each input is allowed, and product thermal inputs attain equality even when their entropies differ.
problem_status_before: Guha–Shapiro entropy photon-number inequality (2008)
rating_reason: Settles a known quantum-Shannon conjecture.

title: Parity is not in QAC0
one_line_claim: Resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model: constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates, unbounded-arity Toffoli gates and polynomially many total qubits cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage.
problem_status_before: Moore's parity-in-QAC⁰ question (1999)
rating_reason: Settles a famous quantum circuit question.

title: QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy
one_line_claim: Proves QMA-hardness of approximating the electronic Coulomb energy infimum in three dimensions, minimizing over the full spinful fermionic continuum space.
problem_status_before: Hamiltonian complexity
rating_reason: Solid complexity result.

title: Classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping
one_line_claim: Determines the unassisted classical capacity of every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel, including all damping and thermal parameters.
problem_status_before: Capacity of a specific channel
rating_reason: Specialist information-theory result.

title: Threshold repetition for entangled games
one_line_claim: Proves exponential threshold repetition for every finite two-player one-round game: if its entangled value is v &lt 1, the probability of winning at least a fraction v+δ of k independent repetitions decays exponentially in k, for 0< δ< 1-v.
problem_status_before: Parallel repetition for entangled games
rating_reason: Solid quantum complexity result.

title: Failure of Kohn–Sham ensemble representation
one_line_claim: Constructs a three-electron Coulomb molecule with two equal positive-integer-charge nuclei whose absolute ground-state density has no noninteracting ground-state ensemble representation by a single real spin-independent local potential in L^3/2(ℝ^3)+L^∞(ℝ^3).
problem_status_before: Kohn–Sham representability
rating_reason: Answers a foundational DFT question negatively.

title: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set
one_line_claim: Gives a polynomial-time uniform quantum circuit family that outputs the complete prime factorization of every integer with probability one.
problem_status_before: Exact (zero-error) Shor factoring
rating_reason: Neat but niche.

title: Unitary vertex operator algebras and conformal nets
one_line_claim: Proves the strongly rational case of the strong-locality conjecture: every simple unitary strongly rational complex vertex operator algebra generates a completely rational conformal net.
problem_status_before: Carpi–Kawahigashi–Longo–Weiner strong locality
rating_reason: Specialist mathematical-physics result.

title: QAOA attains the SK optimum in the thermodynamic-first limit
one_line_claim: Proves that QAOA approaches the ground-state energy of the Gaussian zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model when system size tends to infinity before circuit depth.
problem_status_before: QAOA performance on SK
rating_reason: Solid quantum-algorithms analysis.
verification: Lean, partial (conditional supporting results; QAOA claim unformalized)

title: From scale symmetry to local conformal symmetry in four-dimensional QFT
one_line_claim: Under the stated bounded-local-net and field-reconstruction hypotheses, proves that scale symmetry implies local conformal symmetry for four-dimensional unitary positive-energy theories with a discrete bounded-below scaling spectrum of finite multiplicity, finite scaling support and a physical local scale current.
problem_status_before: Scale vs conformal invariance in 4D (Polchinski 1988)
rating_reason: Partial, under axiomatic hypotheses.

title: Polynomial-time unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle
one_line_claim: Solves the constant-error Aaronson–Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem: a uniform polynomial-size quantum oracle circuit approximates every n-qubit unitary channel within diamond-norm error 1/2, after a suitable Boolean oracle is chosen.
problem_status_before: Aaronson–Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem (2007)
rating_reason: Answers a known quantum-complexity question.

title: The optimal quartic separation between randomized and quantum queries
one_line_claim: Shows that the universal bound R(f)=O((1+Q(f))^4) for total Boolean functions is sharp in its exponent, ruling out every smaller power and disproving the conjectured cubic relation.
problem_status_before: Aaronson et al. (2020) R = O(Q⁴); cubic separation conjectured tight
rating_reason: Settles the randomized–quantum query relationship.

title: Counterexamples to Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky
one_line_claim: Disproves the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes conjecture through a failure of rational injectivity and a separate failure of surjectivity of assembly.
problem_status_before: Baum–Connes without coefficients (1980s) and Kadison–Kaplansky for torsion-free groups
rating_reason: Failure of rational injectivity would also disprove the strong Novikov conjecture for that group; a major shock to noncommutative geometry.

title: Rigidity and arithmetic of lattice von Neumann algebras
one_line_claim: Classifies finite-index bimodules between scalar-twisted group factors of ICC groups commensurable with property-(T) lattices over characteristic-zero local fields and arbitrary ICC group factors.
problem_status_before: Connes' rigidity conjecture for property (T) lattice factors; partial results by Popa, Ioana and others
rating_reason: Rigidity classification for lattice group factors, close to Connes' rigidity conjecture.
notable_flags: Unformalized; scope relative to the full Connes conjecture unclear.

title: Isomorphism of the free group factors
one_line_claim: Resolves the free group factor isomorphism problem: L(𝔽_2)≅ L(𝔽_3), and hence all interpolated free group factors, including L(𝔽_∞), are isomorphic.
problem_status_before: Free group factor isomorphism problem (Murray–von Neumann era); Dykema–Rădulescu dichotomy (1994); many experts expected non-isomorphism
rating_reason: Settles the most famous open problem about II₁ factors, in the less expected direction.
